Browser local storage is acknowledgement state only: its versioned key and runtime envelope both bind tenant, store, user and content type; exact entries live in a capped null-prototype map, malformed/cross-scope rows are evicted, and content/workspace changes reset state before scoped hydration.
8. **Errors/retry/idempotency:** Firestore transaction retries serialize concurrent source/audit writers. The UI lock prevents same-component duplicate taps; there is no global cross-device idempotency receipt. Fixed user errors and bounded hook diagnostics avoid raw persisted content.
9. **Reads/consumers:** Normal article/changelog rendering consumes aggregate counters without audit reads. Owner changelog preview loads at most the latest 100 normalized actor items on demand. No public response includes actor audit identity.
10. **Tests:** Focused runtime/source verifier; rules emulator proves exact append/cap/cross-scope denial and forced malformed-audit rollback of a coupled article counter update; root typecheck/lint.
11. **External proof:** QA rule deployment, authenticated multi-device contention, and hosted browser behavior remain outside local proof.

**Reverse trace:** `kb_articles.likes/dislikes` and `changelog/{tId}/{sId}.entries[].likes/dislikes` reaction writes now have one active browser producer: the coupled content-feedback transaction. The former split article/changelog counter functions and audit-only writer are removed. `article_feedback` and `changelog_feedback` are produced only by that transaction, read on demand through `normalizeContentFeedbackItem()`, and capped without history replacement. FAQ reactions remain a separate single-document transaction and do not create actor audit rows.

### DF-POS-001 — POS full-snapshot delivery and connection test

1. **Trigger/entry:** Successful desktop editor `updateProject()` acknowledgement calls the browser debounce; owners may explicitly call the protected connection-test route.
2. **Auth/authorization:** Both routes use `withAuth()`, feature admission, store permission admission, `verifyTenantAccess()`, and `requireAnyStorePermissionForStoreData()` against the canonical store. Delivery permits integration management or menu publish; test requires integration management.

Public HTTPS syntax and every resolved address are checked. `Project`, `PosSyncConfig`, `PosSyncPayload`, `PosDeliveryLog` and pure delivery-state types describe admitted internal shapes; persisted versions/status inputs are normalized at runtime. Owner history uses a separate allowlisted projector that requires exact document identity, status, timestamp, response and nonnegative numeric fields before state admission.
5. **Normalization/transformation/business rules:** Project top-level extracted data wins when populated, otherwise file data is combined. Category/item IDs are deduplicated, malformed identities are omitted, localized/array/numeric fields are normalized, and only public operational fields are constructed. Decision Fact provenance is excluded. Full snapshots only; no delta or inbound overwrite.
6. **Reads:** Initial `stores/{sId}` admission; `projects/{tId}/{sId}/{projectId}` for delivery; current store transaction reads for configuration/version and completion; `posDeliveryLogs` retention query. Connection test performs a current store re-read before send and a transaction read before status update.
7. **Writes/transactions/batches:** Delivery transaction claims the next safe integer version; a later transaction writes the deterministic delivery log together with any eligible version-ordered status transition and `lastCompletedMenuVersion`. A bounded newest-100 retention scan batch-deletes entries after the newest 20; cleanup failure is logged without changing provider outcome. Test/invalid-target state writes are conditional transactions. Owner connection settings still use the existing store DAL.
8. **Cache/state:** No server/public cache mutation occurs; the upstream project save owns public invalidation. Browser debounce is partitioned by tenant/store/project. Desktop and mobile owner state remounts by exact tenant/store; delivery-history and connection-test settlement is latest-request guarded, sensitive state is discarded on scope change, and functional store-state merges recheck the expected tenant/store. No Redux/SWR/local-storage POS delivery state is authoritative.
9. **Webhook/serialization:** The exact JSON string is HMAC-SHA256 signed. UTF-8 byte length and SHA-256 body hash are logged. The DNS-approved public address set is frozen into a custom Node HTTPS lookup, TLS verifies the configured hostname, timeout is 5 seconds, response body is drained, response headers are capped, and redirects are not followed.
10. **Errors/retry/idempotency/observability:** One attempt only. Receiver ordering/dedupe uses version and delivery ID. First two live failures are logged quietly; the third marks a connection issue. Older completions cannot supersede newer versions. Invalid configuration/test failures mark only the unchanged connection. Bounded diagnostic codes exclude secrets, raw URLs and provider bodies.
11. **Final consumers:** Connected provider, owner delivery history/health, Platform Pull formatter reuse and downstream monitoring.
12. **Tests:** `test:pos-sync-boundaries`, `verify:pos-sync-boundary`, tenant-safety, Platform Pull and Public Business Truth gates, root TypeScript. The source gate pins current-scope history rendering, desktop/mobile keyed remounts, request invalidation and expected-scope state merges.
13. **Unresolved assumptions/external proof:** Real provider TLS/DNS behavior, egress policy, provider dedupe/application, authenticated desktop/mobile history QA, ordered app/rules/legacy-secret rollout, Vercel release and production-host smoke are not locally proven. The inactive `posDeliveryQueue` type/constant was removed on July 16, 2026 rather than retained as dormant architecture.

**Reverse trace:** Non-secret `stores.posSync` is produced by desktop/mobile owner settings plus protected secret/test/delivery transactions and consumed by settings/share status, the loaded-store registration, protected routes and Platform Pull version fallback. Browser consumers attach every local draft, secret, test result, delivery list and completed state patch to the exact tenant/store that produced it; store replacement invalidates or masks older state before consumption. The signing value is server-owned at `posSyncSecrets/{tId}_{sId}` and direct clients are denied. Both acknowledged shared project-DAL save branches feed the browser debounce. `stores/{sId}/posDeliveryLogs` is written only by the protected Admin delivery route, retained to 20, and client-readable only when the parent store exists and both tenant/store claims match (or the session is platform admin); all client writes are denied. Desktop projects valid rows through an owner-safe DTO that excludes error/payload evidence. `PosSyncPayload` is produced by the shared formatter for webhook/test/Pull output and consumed only outside the app boundary after public-safe construction.

### DF-PULL-001 — Platform Pull menu output

1. **Trigger/entry:** External `GET /api/public/v1/business` or `GET /api/public/v1/menu` with `X-API-Key`; authenticated owner `POST /api/store/public-api-key` generates or revokes a key.
2. **Authentication/authorization:** Pull requests first pass a fail-closed HMAC-hashed client-IP ceiling, then exact `ml_` syntax and a fail-closed HMAC-hashed key ceiling. Hash and legacy-raw credential queries each use `limit(2)`; the union must identify exactly one store. Explicit credential product, purpose and scopes must be `ML`, `menulist_public_api` and include `public:read`; metadata-free legacy credentials remain compatible. Key mutation rechecks current tenant/store authority in its transaction.
3. **Tenant/store/project derivation:** Store document identity, every present `tenantId/tId` and `storeId/sId` alias, exact `ML` product admission and canonical tenant lifecycle must agree. Summary map keys select candidate projects; full project document IDs remain authoritative. Linked outlets decode and validate a same-tenant master reference before using the shared master-plus-overrides resolver.
4. **Raw input/runtime type:** Header presence, credential syntax, persisted credential metadata, store/tenant lifecycle, summary rows, project identity, linked-master identity and menu/business values are runtime-admitted. Shared store types use exact product/purpose/scope unions rather than broad strings.
5. **Normalization/transformation/business rules:** Business output allowlists known boolean attributes and only active, valid, bounded temporary status fields. Menu output resolves master, outlet overrides and local records, preserves outlet project identity, and inherits language/version metadata only when absent locally. The existing public menu formatter remains the serialization authority.
6. **Reads/writes/transactions:** Business pull performs two bounded credential queries plus one tenant read. Standalone menu adds one summary and one project read; linked outlet adds one master read. Generate/revoke performs two transactional point reads and one store update. Pulls perform no Firestore write.
7. **Cache/conditional response:** Keyed errors and one-time key responses are `private, no-store`; keyed responses vary on `X-API-Key`. ETag identity excludes request-time `generatedAt`/POS timestamp while 200 bodies retain them, so unchanged truth can return 304 without claiming Firestore-read savings.
8. **Queues/webhooks/public filtering:** No queue or webhook side effect exists. Business and menu serializers omit raw keys, hashes, provider configuration, internal creator fields, arbitrary business attributes and internal intelligence/provenance.
9. **Errors/retry/observability:** Invalid, duplicate, cross-representation or out-of-scope credentials fail non-enumerating. Quota exhaustion is 429; limiter infrastructure failure is retryable 503; both send `Retry-After`. Missing menu is 404; unexpected failures use bounded diagnostics and private no-store errors.
10. **Idempotency:** Pulls are read-only. Key generation returns a one-time raw secret while persisting only its non-secret projection; revocation removes credential material transactionally. Repeated conditional reads use stable truth identity.
11. **Final consumers:** External polling/integration clients, authenticated Business Settings key lifecycle UI and downstream CDN/private intermediary behavior.
12. **Tests:** Platform Pull source/behavior gate covers dual limiter ordering, duplicate/cross-representation credentials, exact identity/metadata, linked outlets, safe business projection, ETags, private errors/secrets and 429/503. Summary, POS, tenant-safety, public-business-truth, auth, type and docs gates cover shared consumers.
13. **Unresolved assumptions/external proof:** Real key provisioning, live provider traffic, authenticated key UI, deployed headers and client polling remain outside local proof. App deployment was not requested.

**Reverse trace:** `stores.publicApi` has one reviewed MenuList writer and is read only by public API authentication/key-management surfaces in this flow; legacy raw/hash representations are queried together and cannot select different stores. `platformSummary/projects_{sId}` producers use the canonical summary writer or supported legacy flat shape; the safe parser rejects prototype paths and yields key-authoritative entries. Selected `projects/{tId}/{sId}/{projectId}` and linked master documents cannot replace identity through embedded fields. The resulting DTOs expose only public business/menu fields and stable response identity.

### DF-CUSTOM-DOMAIN-001 — Owner custom-domain lifecycle to public hostname resolution

1. **Trigger/entry:** Authenticated owner `POST`, `GET` or `DELETE /api/domain`; public requests resolve custom-domain, subdomain or outlet hostname candidates through the two maintained lookup paths.
2. **Authentication/authorization:** Domain mutations derive current user, tenant and store only from the signed session, require exact active/verified membership and domain permission, then re-read canonical tenant/store identity before and during transactional claim work. Public lookup is anonymous but admission-only and fails closed on non-unique or ineligible candidates.
3. **Identity/validation:** Hostnames are canonical DNS names with total/label bounds. Claim documents are deterministic by domain and carry tenant/store plus UUID operation identity. Every present compact/legacy entity alias must agree with canonical document IDs; public store output additionally requires an existing active, non-deleted, non-blocked tenant.
4. **Transactions/concurrency:** Reservation and release leases serialize every store, including overlapping same-store operations. Replacement atomically writes the new current mapping and old-domain `releasing` lease before provider removal. Only the matching reservation may finalize; bounded expired leases recover.
5. **Provider transformations:** Vercel add/config/project/remove calls use manual redirects, bounded bodies and a ten-second deadline that remains active through body parsing. A conflict is accepted only with MenuList provenance plus configured-project proof. GET verification requires explicit DNS configuration and configured-project membership.
6. **Reads/writes/cache:** Mutations use bounded store/domain/claim reads and transactional store plus `platformSummary/customDomainClaim_*` writes. Provider cleanup follows committed claim ordering. Successful current-truth changes invalidate the relevant public store/menu/OBP caches; partial cache/provider/claim-release completion is returned explicitly. Desktop/mobile owner state is keyed by exact tenant/store; status/availability requests are latest-owned and functional state merges recheck the originating scope.
7. **Error/retry/idempotency:** Duplicate legacy rows, owner/claim mismatch and incompatible active leases return 409 before mutation. Provider 404 is idempotent absence. Transport, malformed/empty 200 or stalled bodies become 502/pending state; explicit negative provider truth clears verification, while infrastructure uncertainty preserves last confirmed truth.
8. **Public/private filtering:** Public lookup returns store-safe business truth only; tenant documents are used for admission and are not spread into output. Provider tokens, claim operation IDs and legacy conflict details never enter public DTOs.
9. **Observability:** Diagnostics use bounded domain/state/status booleans and fixed codes; no session, provider secret or raw body is logged.
10. **Final consumers/tests:** Owner desktop/mobile domain settings, middleware/public routing and public store/menu/OBP resolution. The source gate pins keyed remounts, request invalidation and exact-scope state settlement in addition to provider fake-timer/empty-body regression, pure entity identity cases and Firestore-emulator contention/legacy/recovery cases.
11. **Unresolved assumptions/external proof:** Real Vercel project/DNS status, authenticated desktop/mobile conflict QA, normal app release and production-host smoke are external. No Firestore rule/index/Function change was required.

**Reverse trace:** Current custom domain fields are written only by the reviewed owner domain route. Desktop/mobile browser projections bind subdomain/custom-domain drafts, provider/DNS status and completed local merges to the exact current tenant/store; a prior scope cannot become the next store's UI truth. Deterministic claim documents are written by reservation/finalization/release/compensation helpers and read only by those mutation paths. Both public lookup implementations require unique candidates and canonical tenant/store admission before returning store-safe output; neither uses provider state or claim metadata as public content.

### DF-ONBOARD-001 — Global tenant/store identity allocation

1. **Trigger/entry:** Website, reseller, Answerlattice, public-draft and messaging publish transactions create tenant+store scope; platform operators may create a tenant or store manually; authenticated owners may create an outlet.
2. **Auth/authorization:** Onboarding routes keep their existing authenticated/public-claim/provider admission. Manual browser writes require the platform role through Firestore rules. Outlet creation uses `withAuth`, tenant access, outlet permission, bounded input, rate limit, billing capacity and a tenant creation lock.
3. **Identity derivation:** `platformSummary/summary` is canonical. Allocation floors reconcile canonical counters, the legacy read-only `platformSummary/default` counter, and strict positive numeric IDs in `storesSummary`; ambiguous/unsafe values and prototype paths are ignored. Up to 25 candidate entity documents are checked before failure.
4. **Transactions/concurrency:** Manual platform allocation reserves one counter in a retrying client transaction before the entity write, so a failed entity write may leave a harmless gap but cannot reuse the ID. Central onboarding creates the tenant/store and advances both counters in one Admin transaction. Outlet creation probes and creates the store while advancing the store counter in its existing transaction. Concurrent transactions conflict on the canonical summary and retry to distinct IDs.
5. **Reads/writes:** Allocation reads canonical/legacy/store-summary docs plus only occupied candidate entity documents. Successful manual reservation writes the canonical counter once. Central onboarding writes canonical counters, tenant, store and store-summary in one transaction plus caller-owned user/project/subscription work. Outlet creation preserves its existing store/tenant/user/project/summary writes.
6. **Validation/types:** Shared app/Functions counter-boundary files are byte-identical; counters and summary identities accept only exact nonnegative/positive safe integers. The canonical allocator returns a positive number or fails with `platform_counter_allocation_exhausted`.
7. **Errors/idempotency/observability:** Transaction retries handle contention. Twenty-five consecutive occupied candidates fail closed rather than overwrite an entity. Existing bounded route/DAL diagnostics surface failure; no raw entity data is logged.
8. **Consumers/tests:** Tenant/store documents, sessions, project paths, billing and all downstream tenant isolation depend on these IDs. The emulator suite covers legacy/flat floors, magic/ambiguous values, occupied IDs, concurrent platform reservations, concurrent complete onboarding transactions and committed entity documents. Multi-Location, tenant/auth, reseller and Answerlattice source gates cover every active allocator.
9. **External proof:** Current production counter values and successful Functions/Vercel deployment are not locally observable. The Functions QA deploy completed lint/build and then failed Cloud Resource Manager HTTP 403; the app-side release remains opt-in and was not deployed.

**Reverse trace:** Canonical `platformSummary/summary.{tenants,stores}.count` is written only by the shared client reservation adapter, central tenant/store transaction, outlet transaction and legacy Functions publish transaction. All read the same shared floor contract; legacy `default` is read only for compatibility. `tenants/{id}` and `stores/{id}` candidate existence is checked before any counter write, preventing split-counter legacy state from selecting an occupied document.

### DF-MESSAGING-001 — Preview approval to atomic phone-owner business publish

1. **Trigger/entry:** A token holder posts a bounded approve body to `/api/msg-preview/[sessionId]/approve`; the active executor is `src/lib/messaging-onboarding/publish.ts`.
2. **Authentication/authorization:** This public activation route intentionally has no NextAuth session. A 20-256 character preview token is checked against the exact normalized session document inside the initial state transaction; hashed IP publish limiting runs before JSON parsing. The token authorizes only that session.

New messaging and phone-OTP users derive the same `phone_{HMAC(NEXTAUTH_SECRET,user:E164)}` ID and transaction `create` it once.
6. **Reads/writes/transaction order:** The publish transaction reads the session and owner claim before `createTenantStoreInTransaction`; it then writes tenant/store/counters/summary, claimed user, project/project summary and final `LIVE` session state atomically. A stale, mismatched, already-scoped or competing owner claim aborts all business writes.
7. **Cache/public effects:** After commit, menu/store/client-store/screen tags, Digital Screen content version and Owner Business Assistant packet cache are invalidated. Cache failure is bounded and observable but does not reverse committed authoritative truth.
8. **Retries/idempotency/errors:** `LIVE` plus `publishedResult` returns existing success. `PUBLISHING` returns 409. Firestore retries transaction contention. Owner-claim conflict is non-retryable: session returns to `AWAITING_APPROVAL` and the route returns 409. Other publish failures retry once, then recover the session and log a fixed failure code.
9. **Queues/webhooks/observability:** Preview/publish events are best-effort bounded metadata. `confirmationPending` lets the intake scheduler deliver provider confirmation after commit. Logs exclude raw phone/token/provider payload and use bounded IDs/context.
10. **Final consumers/public filtering:** The owner receives public/dashboard URLs only. Public menu/OBP readers consume store/project truth through their own DTO boundaries; no claim token, phone owner record or internal session data enters public output.
11. **Tests:** Messaging source gate, dedicated Firestore emulator concurrent existing/new/scoped/mismatched owner cases, root type/lint/docs/diff and aggregate readiness.
12. **Unresolved:** Authenticated/real preview browser QA, WhatsApp/provider smoke, Vercel release and production-host behavior remain outside local proof. Wider inbound/intake/extraction flow review remains active.

**Reverse trace:** New phone owner IDs are produced only by the shared phone identity helper used by phone OTP and messaging publish. Legacy phone users remain discoverable, but messaging can update one only after the transaction revalidates its exact identity and unscoped state. `users.tenantId/storeId/stores` is coupled to the tenant/store/project/session writes; the losing transaction leaves no partial business. The session `publishedResult.userId` and project `uId` both use the claimed document reference.

### DF-AUTH-STATUS-001 — Session access-status to access-ended browser enforcement

1. **Trigger/entry:** Authenticated desktop/mobile/browser sessions poll `/api/auth/access-status` through `SessionExpiryMonitor`.
2. **Authentication/authorization:** The route uses `withAuth`, same-origin credentials, a hashed user/tenant/store rate limit and no-store response headers. It reads current user truth with the Admin SDK, so Firestore rules are not the route's authorization boundary.
3. **Tenant/store derivation:** User document truth takes precedence over session claims; session tenant/store values are fallback references only. Every referenced document ID is normalized through the shared Firestore document-ID guard before any direct read.
4. **Reads/writes:** The route reads at most one `users`, one `tenants` and one `stores` document and writes nothing. It performs no public-cache, SWR, Redux, local-storage, queue, webhook, billing or publication side effects.
5. **Business rules:** Missing/deleted/inactive/unverified/blocked users fail closed. Invalid tenant/store references fail closed. Non-platform sessions that still reference a tenant or store document fail closed if the document is missing, non-platform store-scoped sessions fail closed when no tenant document was checked, and a store document must normalize `tenantId`/`tId` to the checked tenant document ID before success. Platform sessions retain explicit tolerance for absent platform tenant/store scope, while referenced tenant/store documents still block access when platform-blocked.
6. **Session revocation:** `sessionRevokedAt`, `authTokensRevokedAt` and `accessRevokedAt` are accepted as numeric, Firestore Timestamp-like or canonical ISO timestamps only. A revocation after token issue returns `SESSION_REVOKED`.
7. **Output/private filtering:** Responses are bounded `{valid, reason?, checkedAt?}` no-store JSON. Security logs use bounded route/session/runtime context and do not log raw user, tenant, store or payload data.
8. **Consumer/concurrency behavior:** `SessionExpiryMonitor` maps stale tenant/store and store-tenant mismatch reasons to the same owner-safe access-ended modal as other account-access changes. Each poll is bound to exact user/tenant/store/product/role/expiry identity and a monotonic request token. A session/request replacement or effect cleanup invalidates older work before it can display the modal or call sign-out.
9. **Tests:** Auth/security and tenant-safety source gates pin document-ID normalization, platform tolerance, missing tenant/store fail-closed reasons, normalized store-to-tenant comparison, browser reason mapping and docs/changelog evidence. The shared latest-request behavior suite proves request replacement and cleanup invalidation. Root TypeScript, lint, docs links, audit tooling and diff integrity are required for closure.
10. **Unresolved:** Authenticated hosted browser polling, rapid two-account response-order smoke, deleted-tenant/store live-data inventory and deployed Vercel behavior remain outside local source proof.

**Reverse trace:** `valid: true` is now produced only after current user admission, optional tenant/store document existence for non-platform sessions, required tenant context for non-platform store-scoped sessions, store-to-tenant ownership coherence when both exist, blocked-entity checks and session-revocation comparison. The browser access-ended modal consumes only the current request's reason code; no tenant/store document fields are serialized to the client, and a prior session's response cannot become current sign-out authority.

### DF-AUTH-CLAIM-001 — One-time messaging owner claim to real login account

1. **Trigger/entry:** The responsive login page posts one bounded Google, email/password, or WhatsApp/passcode claim to `/api/auth/claim-account` after `validate-claim` acknowledgement.
2. **Authentication/authorization:** Modes 2/3 use the 256-bit claim token as authority; Google additionally requires a current NextAuth session. Hashed-IP `AUTH_SENSITIVE` limiting and a 16 KiB body cap precede token lookup.
3. **Raw input/validation:** Shared claim-token syntax is 20-256 base64url/hex-safe characters. Mode schemas bound email, password and name. Google user ID must be an exact Firestore document ID and its normalized session email must pass email validation.
4. **Reservation before side effects:** `reserveClaimAccountOperation()` transactionally re-reads the messaging user and rejects missing/stale/malformed/expired token, inactive/blocked/deleted/Auth-disabled user, malformed tenant/store IDs, missing exact owner mapping or a live 15-minute competing reservation. Only the winner can create or update Firebase Auth.
5. **Canonical target identity:** Phone/passcode retains the canonical phone user. Email/password derives the same hashed global-email document ID used by first OAuth sign-in and transaction-creates that target while retiring the phone source. Google re-reads its exact session user target and rejects different email, any tenant/store/mapping, inactive/block/deletion/Auth-disabled state or privileged non-owner/user platform role.
6. **Auth side effects/compensation:** Email creates a Firebase Auth identity. Phone may update an existing generated-email identity only after its UID/email queries prove no different user binding. If finalization fails, request-created Auth deletion first queries all user bindings plus the source; only an unbound UID is compensatable. The exact reservation is released without consuming the token.
7. **Final transaction/reads/writes:** Finalization re-reads the token/reservation, canonical tenant and store identity/status, target user where applicable, and at most 101 subscriptions. Above 100 fails closed. It atomically writes target/source user ownership, tenant/store email when applicable, every admitted subscription link, token consumption and reservation deletion.
8. **Cache/state/custom claims:** Mode 1/2 store email changes revalidate public menu/OBP/store/client-store truth after commit. Mode 2/3 custom claims mirror after commit. Mirror failure emits bounded diagnostics and returns committed success; the normal credential sign-in `/api/auth/set-claims` path repairs the mirror.
9. **Concurrency/retry/idempotency:** Concurrent reservations produce one winner before password/Auth mutation. Firestore retries final read/write conflicts. A stale token/operation or canonical scope change returns generic conflict. A failed final transaction keeps the token recoverable after operation-specific release. A completed token cannot be replayed.
10. **Output/private filtering:** Success returns only mode and numeric tenant/store identity plus fixed copy. Errors are generic and logs use bounded request/token presence-length context; password, token, raw email/phone and provider objects are not logged.
11. **Consumers/tests:** NextAuth credentials/Google sessions, Firebase client claim sync, owner dashboard, subscriptions and public store email/cache consumers. Dedicated Firestore emulator covers competing reservation, final rollback/release, canonical email target, subscription coupling, malformed expiry, block state, global Auth compensation binding and Google target admission; auth/tenant/public source gates pin order and fields.
12. **Unresolved:** Firebase Auth emulator provider mutation/cleanup, hosted parallel claim attempts, browser/mobile claim flow and Vercel release remain outside local proof.

**Reverse trace:** `users.claimToken/claimOperation` are written by messaging publish/reservation and consumed only through the claim boundary. Mode 2's canonical global-email target and Mode 1's Google target become the authoritative login user; their `claimedFrom` points to the retired phone source. Mode 3 updates that phone source in place. `subscriptions.userId/email/name` changes are now written only inside the same final claim transaction for this flow. Firebase custom claims are a recoverable mirror, not the ownership authority.

### DF-ROUTE-001 — Durable public-subdomain ownership

1. **Trigger/entry:** Central onboarding may allocate a requested/fallback host; authenticated owners check and assign an unpublished store host through `/api/subdomain/check`; platform operators use `/api/admin/subdomains/rename` for governed published-store exceptions.
2. **Auth/authorization:** The owner routes use `withAuth`, bounded hashed rate limits, `MANAGE_PUBLIC_PRESENCE`, exact session tenant/store scope, and transactional main-location authority. Explicit outlets are denied; unmarked legacy stores are admitted only when bounded canonical queries prove a unique single-store tenant. The admin route requires the platform role, strict positive tenant/store document IDs, a reason, and acknowledgement reference. Central onboarding retains each caller's existing admission and atomically creates the new tenant/store.
3. **Identity/validation:** DNS labels are slug-normalized, reserved names are rejected, and the shared claim boundary admits only 3-63 character lowercase labels. Canonical `stores/{storeId}` identity is re-read transactionally; owner scope must match the session tenant and admin scope must match the requested tenant.
4. **Reads/transactions:** Availability is decided from deterministic `platformSummary/subdomainClaim_{subdomain}`, a bounded current-owner query, and a bounded redirect-history query in the same Firestore transaction that owns the mutation. Advisory GET/precheck repeats those reads but cannot reserve a name. The compatibility queries protect legacy stores that predate claim documents.
5. **Writes:** Onboarding writes the new store and current claim atomically. Owner assignment writes store, `storesSummary`, and current claim, releasing a valid prior unpublished claim. Platform rename writes store/history, summary, audit row, new current claim, and valid prior redirect claim atomically. Malformed legacy slugs are preserved in canonical history but never interpolated into deterministic claim document IDs.
6. **Concurrency/idempotency:** Firestore retries conflicting transactions. A claim owned by another store, any other canonical owner, active history owner, malformed non-expiring foreign claim, or saturated history query fails closed. Reassigning the same store to its current host is idempotent for owners; admin no-op/stale-scope retries return conflict rather than a false server fault.
7. **Cache/consumers:** Successful owner/admin changes invalidate menu/store/client-store/screen tags and refresh Digital Screen and Owner Business Assistant projections after commit. Middleware/public store resolution continues to consume canonical store/redirect fields, which the claim boundary keeps unique.
8. **Errors/observability:** Unavailable and published-lock conflicts are 409, stale owner scope is 403, malformed input is 400, and unexpected failures emit bounded security diagnostics without raw store documents or session data.
9. **Tests:** The Firestore emulator proves two concurrent onboarding transactions receive distinct hosts and two existing stores racing for one host produce exactly one canonical/claim owner. Pure assertions cover 63/64-character and malformed legacy labels. URL-routing and API tenant-safety source gates pin auth, transaction, claim, cache, and no-preflight-query invariants.
10. **External proof:** This is app/server-route source. Vercel deployment was not authorized; authenticated owner/platform browser QA, concurrent live-project smoke, and production-host lookup remain pending.

**Reverse trace:** `stores.subdomain` is produced by central onboarding and the two protected assignment routes; browser DAL updates delegate it to the owner POST and remove it from direct client writes. `platformSummary/subdomainClaim_*` is written only by those transactional producers and has no public reader. `stores.previousSubdomains`/`previousSubdomainSlugs` is written only by the admin rename route and consumed by legacy public redirect lookup plus the transactional compatibility check. `storesSummary.stores.{storeId}.subdomain` is updated in the same owner/admin transaction and remains a derived internal read model, not public routing authority.

### DF-MULTI-001 — Outlet creation, path rename, and deactivation

1. **Trigger/entry:** An authenticated master-store owner creates, renames, or deactivates an outlet from desktop/mobile Locations through the protected outlet routes.
2. **Auth/authorization:** Feature flags, exact session tenant/store document IDs, tenant access, HMAC-hashed tenant rate limits, bounded JSON/Zod admission, canonical master-store reads, `MANAGE_OUTLETS`, and canonical target tenant/master/active status precede mutation.
3. **Identity/validation:** Global store IDs come from the shared transactional counter. Outlet path segments are slug-normalized, reserved names rejected, capped at 60 characters, and claimed under exact tenant scope. Different tenants may reuse a segment; stores inside one tenant may not.
4. **Reads/transactions:** Creation prefetches project templates and billing state, but re-reads canonical counter, tenant, summary, user and candidate store documents in the creation transaction. Create/rename reads deterministic `outletSlugClaim_{tenantId}_{slug}` plus bounded current/history compatibility queries before any write. Rename re-reads target outlet and tenant inside its transaction. Deactivation re-reads target/tenant and the current claim before writes.
5. **Writes:** Creation writes outlet, current claim, summary, tenant list, user access, counter and replicated project summaries in one transaction after provider capacity succeeds. Rename writes outlet/history, current/redirect claims, summary and tenant list atomically. Deactivation writes inactive store, released current claim, summary and tenant list atomically; provider subscription reconciliation follows its documented compensation path.
6. **Concurrency/idempotency:** The creation lock controls billing/create overlap, the tenant read prevents lost `storesList` updates, and deterministic slug claims serialize create/rename competitors. Same-tenant conflicts return 409; a saturated 20-row history range fails closed. Already-inactive deactivation is idempotent. Claim release permits canonical current-path reuse while permanent rename history remains reserved.
7. **Cache/side effects:** After commit, menu/store/client-store/screen tags, Digital Screen content versions and Owner Business Assistant packets are invalidated. Provider quantity changes occur before internal creation and retain explicit compensation diagnostics if internal creation fails.
8. **Consumers/tests:** Public `getStoreByOutletSlug`, outlet OBP/menu paths, Brand OBP location links, tenant stores list, sessions, summaries, billing capacity and mobile/desktop Locations consume the state. Emulator cases cover same/cross-tenant concurrency and release/reclaim; Multi-Location, tenant-safety and Public Business Truth gates cover source/caches.
9. **External proof:** Razorpay sandbox, authenticated desktop/mobile Locations QA, live-project contention, Vercel deployment and production-host outlet routing remain outside local proof.

**Reverse trace:** `stores.outletSlug` is produced only by outlet create/rename; `previousOutletSlugs` by rename; `platformSummary/outletSlugClaim_*` by create/rename/deactivate. Public resolution queries canonical active stores by tenant+current/history slug. `tenants.storesList` and `storesSummary` are derived in the same transaction as each canonical lifecycle mutation. Deactivation releases only a same-store/absent current claim and retains history reservations.

**Master operational signal subflow:** A successful operational master-project save performs one post-project client write to `masterOperationalState/{masterProjectId}` using atomic `increment(1)` plus `serverTimestamp()`. Firestore rules require current master-store owner/manager authority (or platform admin), exact project tenant/store document scope, exact two-field state, create-at-1 and update-at-current+1. Same-tenant outlets can read the direct document for awareness but cannot mutate another store's signal. Link/switch baseline reads and the visibility-aware `onSnapshot` listener share `parseMasterOperationalState()`; invalid rows are observed and excluded. A newer valid version triggers one debounced master fetch/diff. The listener keeps current same-project snapshot/override data without reconnecting, cancels superseded fetches by request generation, rechecks identity after awaits and clears project-specific refs/state before a new outlet listener becomes actionable. Acknowledgement writes the outlet project snapshot and local state, not the signal. No public cache or DTO consumes this collection.

### DF-CMI-001 — Settled compact analytics and current catalog to private intelligence

1. **Trigger/auth/authorization:** `computeDecisionBlocksScores` runs hourly and processes only due active stores. `triggerStoreNightlyScheduler` is the current-platform one-store recovery entry. The scheduler/Admin SDK owns reads and writes; direct Firestore client reads require the platform claim, and every client write is denied.
2. **Tenant/store/project derivation:** Store and project identity comes from the current platform/store/project summaries and nested project document path. One helper validates canonical positive safe-integer tenant/store IDs, a slash-free bounded project segment and the composite Firestore byte limit before any document reference is constructed, then binds `menuIntelligence/{tId}_{sId}_{projectId}`. Request-supplied identity cannot create an app-side read because the uncertified DAL performs no Firestore operation.
3. **Compact analytics admission:** `analytics/{tId}_{sId}_{projectId}_intelligence_7d` is accepted only when its tenant, store, project, writer kind, exact seven-day start/end range and requested last-settled local date agree. Totals and item/hour maps require non-negative safe integers, bounded safe item keys, canonical hour normalization and bounded names. Missing, stale, malformed, future or cross-scope input returns the existing empty `missing_or_stale` DTO.
4. **Catalog extraction/normalization:** The live project catalog is authoritative. Only active current items enter scoring; retained aliases may merge analytics continuity, but analytics-only/deleted IDs cannot create candidates. Prototype-sensitive, control-character, whitespace-variant and overlong IDs are excluded. Counts are safe integers, owner boost is clamped, names are bounded, hours are canonical, and duplicate current catalog IDs resolve through the extractor map.
5. **Transformation/business logic:** Decision Blocks consumes the same projected analytics and catalog-first extraction for its customer-safe project projection. CMI independently rechecks persistence identity, analytics calendar date, safe item IDs, uniqueness and the 2,000-item ceiling before deriving confidence, priority, ranks, time/suppression metadata, calibration, health and bounded audit entries. Missing/same-date data does not advance maturity; older analytics throws before replacing current evidence, so `lastAnalyticsDate` is monotonic.
6. **Persisted-state projector:** Every existing CMI document must match document identity, exact known fields, safe/bounded related item maps, contiguous ranks, calibration, stats, health, calendar date, Timestamp ordering, bounded audit shapes and cross-field counter relationships. The exported pure computation repeats that exact projection for any direct non-null prior-state argument. Invalid, foreign or legacy-incompatible state throws `menu_intelligence_invalid_persisted_state` and is not overwritten silently.
7. **Atomicity/idempotency/concurrency:** `computeAndPersistMenuIntelligence()` performs transaction get -> strict projection -> request-local audit context -> compute -> complete `transaction.set`. Scheduled/manual overlap retries against current truth, so both runs increment `runCount` without double-aging one settled date or losing audit lineage. Same-date recomputation refreshes operational timestamp/TTL but not confidence age, stable days, calibration or top-item days.
8. **Outputs/cache/public separation:** Raw CMI contains private confidence, suppression and audit evidence. The application DAL is neutral and public/owner/mobile surfaces do not read it. Public menus consume only the separate allowlisted `project.publicDecisionBlocks`; its existing scheduler/manual cache invalidation remains independent. CMI itself has no Redux, SWR, local-storage, public cache, queue, webhook, billing or provider side effect.
9. **Errors/observability/cost:** Malformed compact input follows the existing missing/stale warning path; malformed prior CMI aborts the project computation instead of replacing evidence. Normal CMI cost is one transaction read and one replacement write per enabled active project, plus the already shared compact analytics/project reads. No broad query or per-item document fan-out is added.
10. **Tests/external proof:** The pure boundary matrix covers unsafe/duplicate/path IDs, fractional counts, invalid dates, cross-scope/malformed snapshots, exact persisted projection, same-date maturity and zero-day health. Admin emulators prove compact-snapshot pruning, concurrent scheduled/manual serialization and malformed-state preservation. The rules emulator proves platform-only read and universal client-write denial. Exact TypeScript, Functions build, scoped lint and source verification pass locally. QA rules/indexes/Functions deployment remains blocked by missing Firebase CLI authentication; the pending command is `firebase deploy --project menulist-qa --config firebase.json --only firestore:rules,firestore:indexes,functions:computeDecisionBlocksScores,functions:triggerStoreNightlyScheduler,functions:triggerCustomerAnalyticsManually --non-interactive`.

**Reverse trace:** The compact analytics document is exact-replaced by dashboard settlement and read only by shared Decision Blocks/CMI aggregation through the projector; stale map keys and unknown legacy fields are pruned on every settlement. `menuIntelligence` is written only by the Admin transaction helper, read by that strict Admin projector and separately authorized platform diagnostics, and has no app/public serializer. `project.publicDecisionBlocks` is the only customer-facing derivative; CMI state does not flow into it after computation and no CMI cache key exists.

### DF-OWNER-CONTROL-001 — Confirmed owner-control mutation to authority-maturation summary

1. **Trigger/auth/authorization:** Owner boost, Decision Block and Digital Screen controls call the feature-gated browser DAL under the active session. One exact document ID, `{tId}_{sId}`, owns the store aggregate; document data must contain the same string IDs. Client reads return an allowlisted partial-map DTO; malformed/legacy rows are observed and excluded rather than defaulting to current dates or raw maps.
4. **Writes/transactions/rules:** The five-second per-control debounce retains one write per burst. The write itself is a Firestore transaction: it reads current truth, creates one exact server-timestamped row if absent, or advances one lifetime counter, matching last-used timestamp and current UTC-month counter atomically. Concurrent first controls retry against the created row instead of last-writer replacement. A permission denial after the local UTC month changes retries once with the new month; other denials and second failures propagate. The daily `insights/authority_maturation_YYYY-MM-DD` summary is exact-replaced, so unknown legacy summary fields do not survive.
6. **Cost/cache/public behavior:** Successful control usage remains one aggregate write after one transaction read; first creation is one read/one write. The daily task keeps the same total document-read cost but bounded memory/page size. No public cache, menu, OBP, customer DTO, billing, queue, webhook or provider side effect consumes this collection.
7. **Errors/retry/idempotency/observability:** Browser tracking remains non-blocking and emits stable bounded diagnostics. Firestore transaction retries serialize contention; the one explicit permission-denied retry is admitted only when the UTC month actually changed between attempt and rejection. Invalid persisted state is never overwritten silently. Scheduler logs aggregate processed/invalid/phase counts and retains the outer leased retry/run-log behavior.
8. **Tests/external proof:** The focused emulator proves exact create/update, added-control and repeated-control behavior, parser/mirror integrity, UTC rollover key/retry admission, same-store reads, cross-scope/staff denial, counter/time/identity/field/delete rejection. The source gate pins transaction ordering, runtime projection, UTC/server-time rules, bounded pagination, exact summary replacement and post-success Digital Screen tracking. Exact root TypeScript, Functions build, scoped lint and adjacent master/POS rules emulators pass. QA Firestore rules and Functions deployment remain blocked by missing Firebase CLI authentication; the pending exact command is `firebase deploy --project menulist-qa --config firebase.json --only firestore:rules,functions:computeDecisionBlocksScores --non-interactive`. No Vercel deploy is involved.

**Reverse trace:** `ownerControlUsage/{tId}_{sId}` is produced only by the browser transaction helper and legacy/Admin history, read by the owner stats DAL and Authority Maturation task, and has no public serializer. Its derived daily insight is written only by Admin Functions and consumed as internal maturity evidence; no client writer exists for the insight. Existing valid legacy aggregate rows remain writable through the same transaction; malformed rows require an explicit Admin repair/migration and are otherwise skipped.

### DF-STAFF-001 — Staff identity, store assignment and role lifecycle

1. **Trigger/entry:** Authenticated owner/master users list, create, edit, deactivate, remove, reset or sign out staff through `/api/staff` and its password/sign-out routes; authorized users save/deactivate role definitions through `/api/staff/roles`; platform operators may block/unblock a user through Platform Entity Blocks.

Platform block uses `withPlatformAuth`. Non-master managers can affect only their active session store; identifiers from input are independently validated.
3. **Tenant/store/entity derivation:** Tenant/store request IDs are positive safe integers. Stored/session IDs re-enter `normalizeStaffScopeNumericId`; document refs use canonical document IDs. Target users must belong to the exact tenant. Store docs must be same-tenant, active, not deleted and not platform blocked.
4. **Raw input/runtime validation/type:** Bounded 16KB bodies precede Zod schemas. User document IDs must remain exact, bounded valid Firestore IDs. Mapping arrays are unique and capped at 25. Role IDs/names/descriptions/permission maps are bounded. `CreateStaffInput`, `UpdateStaffInput`, mapping, response and role types describe only admitted data.
5. **Normalization/transformation/business rules:** Mapping roles must exist and be active on fresh stores; stored mapping names always come from canonical store names. Legacy numeric-string mappings normalize only when their decimal representation is canonical. Existing default store remains selected while still assigned. Self-removal/deactivation is denied. Ordinary mutations cannot leave a store without an active unblocked owner.
6. **Reads/writes:** Staff list performs bounded current-store user queries plus eligible store reads. Mutations read the deterministic user, relevant stores and private access-state docs. New staff claim `users/{firebaseUid}`; existing user mutations update one user. Role mutations update one store. Each affected store receives one private state revision write.
7. **Transactions/batches/idempotency:** `staffStoreAccessState/{tenantId}_{storeId}` serializes active `{userId,role}` assignments. It lazy-initializes once from compatible current users. Deterministic create uses transaction `create`; replay conflicts. Mapping/active changes, owner removal, role mutation and platform block/unblock share state read/write conflicts. Firestore retries prevent lost arrays and assignment/deactivation races.
8. **Auth/provider side effects:** Mapping changes revoke Firebase refresh tokens and persist revocation metadata. Deactivation/removal mirrors disabled state after fail-closed Firestore truth commits. New Auth identities are deleted only when that request created the identity and initial persistence fails. Passcode reset uses a leased Firestore reservation before provider mutation and matching finalization after it.
9. **Cache/state/public filtering:** No public cache or DTO consumes the private state. Desktop/mobile clients update local staff rows only after operation-specific response mode and matching user acknowledgement. Returned staff DTOs filter mappings to the caller-visible store set and omit password/passcode/provider/internal state.
10. **Errors/retry/observability:** Invalid, forbidden, missing, duplicate, last-owner and role-in-use paths have stable HTTP statuses/codes. Transaction retries are bounded by Firestore; dynamic legacy guard expansion is capped. Security and lifecycle diagnostics use bounded context and never log passcodes, raw staff payloads, emails/phones or provider objects.
11. **Final consumers:** NextAuth/access-status authorization, owner desktop/mobile staff management, per-store permission calculation and platform support controls.
12. **Tests:** Staff scope behavioral test; dedicated concurrency source gate; Firestore emulator concurrent add/create/owner/block/role cases; Staff/Roles parity; tenant-safety; platform entity-block; root type/lint/docs/diff and aggregate readiness.
13. **Unresolved assumptions/external proof:** Auth-emulator/provider failure injection, authenticated desktop/mobile contention and deployed Vercel behavior remain pending. The private state has no client rule path and is denied by the existing catch-all default-deny rule; no rule/index/Function source changed.

**Reverse trace:** `users.stores[]/storeIds[]/storeId` staff writes now pass through deterministic creation or the shared user mutation transaction. `stores.roles[]` owner-admin writes pass through the shared role transaction; default-role compatibility repair remains a one-time separate store normalization before assignment. `staffStoreAccessState` is produced only by its initializer, staff create/mutation/role boundaries and Platform Entity Blocks synchronization, read only by those Admin helpers, contains no public/profile data, and has no client writer, deleter, cache or public serializer.

### DF-SIGNALDESK-WEBHOOK-001 — Provider event and signed outcome ingestion

1. **Trigger/entry:** Email, WhatsApp, Instagram or Messenger submits a provider callback to the provider webhook route, or an external routed surface submits a signed outcome to the outcome bridge. GET challenge verification is separate from POST ingestion.
2. **Authentication/admission:** Public IP key material is hashed into a fail-closed rate limit before a 256 KiB bounded raw-body read. Provider-specific signatures/verify tokens or HMAC timestamp/signature checks precede database access. Caller limit is 429; limiter/transient persistence failure is 503 with `Retry-After`; responses are no-store.
3. **Raw runtime contract:** Strict provider parsers require object-shaped bodies and one to 100 normalized events. Official Meta message/status arrays and email event shapes are projected into bounded provider/event/external/identity/target/time/text/media facts; unknown outcome fields, malformed timestamps/signatures and oversized values are rejected.
4. **Identity/target derivation:** Email/phone/channel identities resolve transactionally, including canonical `+E.164` and compatible digit-only variants. A supplied target must exist, be safe and equal identity-derived ownership. DNC/complaint suppression can persist at identity scope with `targetId:null` before a target exists.
5. **Idempotency/order:** Provider-scoped path-safe event IDs plus a fingerprint bind normalized facts. Exact duplicates return duplicate; same ID with changed facts returns 409. Every event in a bounded batch runs independently. Late evidence is marked out-of-order and retained without regressing current conversation/target state.
6. **Transactions/writes:** Event reservation is transaction-create atomic with admitted conversation/message/classification/queue/suppression/audit/health/cost/control writes. Inbox backlog changes only when entering/leaving queue state and never below zero. Status callbacks remain status evidence and never become inbound replies. Interested replies reuse the revenue qualification projection path.
7. **Outcome token/transaction:** The outcome bridge verifies HMAC and strict payload, then the outcome transaction rechecks route-token scope, hash, target, status, revocation and expiry. Exact idempotent replay is recognized before revocation denial; new use of revoked/expired token fails. Accepted outcome, summary, route-use update and deterministic direct attribution touch commit atomically.
8. **Private/public fields:** Raw signatures, HMAC secret, raw route token, unrestricted provider payload and unbounded text/media are never persisted or logged. Non-text messages store bounded markers/truncation metadata. SignalDesk is an internal separate surface; no MenuList tenant/public menu DTO or cache is written.
9. **Failures/retries/observability:** Stable parse/shape/conflict/target failure codes classify caller errors; unexpected persistence remains retryable. Bounded diagnostics carry provider/error code and presence/length metadata only. Each batch event can succeed/duplicate/fail independently without acknowledging uncommitted work.
10. **Consumers:** SignalDesk conversations/inbox/target summaries, suppression imports, channel/control/cost health, audit/incident views, revenue accounts/opportunities/activation watch and outcome attribution consumers.
11. **Tests:** `verify:signaldesk` runs 2,466 source checks. Isolated Firestore E2E covers batched Meta events, exact/changed replay, unresolved suppression, canonical phone identity, out-of-order evidence, qualification, signed outcome attribution/revocation/replay and retry statuses. Firestore/Storage rules suite, exact TypeScript, scoped lint and diff integrity pass.
12. **Unresolved/external:** No rules/index/Function source changed in this slice, so no Firebase deploy applies. Vercel was not authorized. Deployed secrets, live Meta/email callbacks, MenuList producer wiring and live retry/status smoke remain external.

**Reverse trace:** `signaldeskWebhookEvents` is the immutable provider fact/idempotency root; conversation/message/classification/suppression/queue/health/cost/audit/control projections are transaction consumers. `signaldeskRouteTokens` authorizes one versioned direct outcome scope and records use/revocation; `signaldeskOutcomeEvents`/summaries plus `signaldeskAttributionTouches` are atomically produced from an admitted signed outcome. Raw route tokens and signatures are verification inputs only and have no persisted/public consumer.

### DF-OPS-NOTIFICATION-001 — Platform/owner notification monitoring and action

1. **Trigger/entry:** Platform operators read recent platform alerts or MenuList/Answerlattice owner-delivery events, inspect one event, acknowledge/mute/toggle SAFE_MODE, retry a failed delivery, or record/send a manual handoff through the four `/api/ops` routes and their desktop monitors.
2. **Authentication/authorization:** `withAuth` establishes a platform session. Separate HMAC-derived read/action limits fail closed before Firestore work and distinguish caller exhaustion (`429`) from limiter infrastructure failure (`503`). Every route then re-reads exact current `users/{uId}` truth; malformed lifecycle/block markers, role/identity mismatch and post-issuance revocation fail closed.
3. **Scope/product derivation:** Platform alert scope is allowlisted/bounded. Owner event product is exact MenuList or Answerlattice; tenant/store/workspace IDs and trigger identity are runtime-normalized from the selected persisted event before delivery work. Cross-product rows never enter a product response.
4. **Reads/queries/cost:** Each monitor uses one bounded newest-first event window and derives recent counts/filtered rows from that same window. Selected owner detail uses `eventId ASC, createdAt DESC, limit(12)`. Recipient scope resolution reports completed reads even when a later legacy fallback fails and returns a fixed detail error instead of silent omission.
5. **Runtime DTO/private filtering:** Persisted event/delivery/alert data is projected through bounded text, exact enum and non-negative safe-integer guards. Malformed role/status/channel values remain explicit `invalid`; private operator identity, raw destination, provider error and unsafe metadata do not cross the response boundary.
6. **Writes/transactions/idempotency:** SAFE_MODE/mute/acknowledgement no-ops do not write. Stable action IDs and deterministic event/delivery IDs make identical manual alert/send/handoff replays no-write/no-redelivery. Manual handoff creates the delivery and marks the source event in one transaction. Current canonical user ID/time provide audit attribution.
7. **Retry/error semantics:** Only claimable failed owner events are offered for retry. Missing/wrong-product returns 404; concurrent/exhausted/unclaimable state returns 409; success is emitted only after a claim/process result supports it. SAFE_MODE state remains successful if its best-effort alert write fails, with separate bounded diagnostics.
8. **Queues/providers/cache:** Manual send and retry reuse the owner-notification processor's claim/delivery path; provider acceptance remains outside Firestore atomicity. These private ops paths do not mutate public menu truth or caches. SAFE_MODE changes operational config only.
9. **Consumers/tests:** Platform Ops Control Room and notification monitors consume bounded acknowledgements and recent-window cost labels. Current-user pure/Admin-emulator, snapshot/window, delivery-boundary and four focused source gates pass; two independent scoped re-reviews found no further defect.

**Reverse trace:** `systemAlerts`, `ownerNotificationEvents` and `ownerNotificationDeliveries` are written by their existing operational/provider producers. Manual action rows carry deterministic action identity and current operator attribution; transaction/replay checks prevent the monitoring surface from becoming a duplicate-delivery writer. Product-specific databases remain separate.

### DF-RESELLER-PAYMENT-001 — Reseller offline-payment confirmation

1. **Trigger/entry:** An authenticated reseller or platform operator posts a bounded `{subscriptionId, confirmed:true}` request to `/api/reseller/confirm-payment` after collecting an offline payment.
2. **Authentication/authorization:** `withAuth` establishes a signed reseller/platform session. A hashed-identity `DATA_WRITE` limit runs before body parsing and database reads. Immediately before the mutation, reseller callers re-read an active exact-email/current-profile identity and platform callers re-read the exact current platform user, including lifecycle, block, role, issuance and revocation state.
3. **Tenant/store/entity derivation:** The caller cannot supply tenant, store, reseller, amount, currency, plan or product. Those values come only from the transaction snapshot. Every present long/compact tenant and store alias must be an exact positive canonical document ID and agree; the stored reseller must be an exact Firestore ID and equal the current reseller actor unless current platform authority was proved.
4. **Raw input/runtime type:** The existing Zod schema follows an exact 16 KiB body cap. The transaction uses `ManualSubscriptionConfirmationAdmission`, whose runtime projector admits only MenuList product identity, manual billing, integer nonnegative paise, `INR`, a bounded plan ID and at most 199 existing status entries.
5. **Business rules/transformation:** Only `pending` plus false/absent confirmation state is eligible. Active plus confirmed is an idempotent replay. Active-unconfirmed, cancelled, completed, expired, past-due, online, foreign-reseller, wrong-product, alias-disagreeing and malformed rows return a bounded non-success result without mutation.
6. **Reads/writes/transaction:** One current-authority read precedes one transaction point read of `subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`. First success merge-writes active status, confirmation timestamp/marker and one status-history row atomically. Firestore retries contention; all competitors re-read the winning active state and write nothing.
7. **Derived/cache effects:** First success and idempotent replay both invoke the existing safe store-plan entitlement/public-assistant cache reconciliation and idempotent owner-referral settlement with only transaction-normalized tenant/store/plan identity. A committed response loss therefore remains recoverable.
8. **Serialization/private filtering:** Success emits only acknowledgement, subscription ID, active status and replay flag. Persisted subscription history, reseller identity, amount, currency and internal repair details are not serialized. Errors are fixed/bounded; diagnostics use bounded identifier context.
9. **Retries/idempotency/failure:** Eight concurrent emulator calls produce one write and seven successful replays with exactly one active history row. Post-commit repair failure preserves the committed subscription and returns a retryable server error; replay reruns repair without another financial transition.
10. **Tests/consumers:** Pure admission tests cover legacy aliases, malicious/malformed state and terminal statuses; Admin Firestore emulator covers concurrency, replay, foreign ownership and no-mutation failures; the reseller source gate pins current authority, transaction ownership and docs parity. Subscription/entitlement/public cache, referral settlement and reseller UI are final consumers.
11. **Unresolved/external:** Authenticated reseller/platform browser smoke and deployed app behavior require the normal Vercel release path, which was not authorized. No provider, rules, index, Function or Storage change is involved.

**Reverse trace:** `subscriptions.status/manualPaymentConfirmed/manualPaymentConfirmedAt/statuses[]` for this endpoint are now produced through one transaction from a single current snapshot. The route cannot overwrite caller-selected fields. Active truth feeds the existing entitlement/public-assistant cache mirror and referral settlement; those are recovery consumers, not authorization sources. Existing online webhooks, renewal and scheduler writers remain separate billing flows and cannot enter this endpoint unless the persisted row is exact manual/pending MenuList truth.

### DF-AUTH-CLIENT-SESSION-001 — Raw browser session to current store and product scope

1. **Trigger/entry:** Browser consumers call `getActiveSession()`. A server render delegates to NextAuth directly; the browser fetches `/api/auth/session` with same-origin credentials, no-store cache policy, manual redirects and a 64 KiB response ceiling.
2. **Authentication/authority:** The route response is the signed NextAuth session source. A browser `activeStoreContext` value is never authority: it can only select a store already present in the signed user's exact mapped-store set.
3. **Raw input/runtime boundary:** Before JWT creation, persisted current-user `tenantId`, `storeId`, `storeIds[]` and `stores[].storeId` pass one exact canonical positive-safe-integer projector; compatible canonical numeric strings become numbers, while exponents, whitespace, leading zeros, decimals and unsafe integers are omitted rather than coerced into membership. The response is then reconstructed as the compact JSON session—not a Firestore `UserDataType`: expiry must be a valid string date, lifecycle fields retain boolean kinds, product IDs and product-account keys are registered values, store arrays are exact, contradictory duplicate roles fail, and top-level user/scope/role/product aliases must agree with the nested user. Explicit null tenant/store is accepted only as the compatible pre-onboarding shape. Active-store JSON must contain only positive safe-integer numeric `tenantId`, `baseStoreId` and `storeId`; strings, exponents, leading-zero legacy forms, missing fields and arrays are rejected.
4. **Tenant/store derivation:** Top-level and nested session tenant/store aliases must all be valid and equal. Persisted context tenant/base store must equal those aliases, and `canUserAccessStore()` must prove the target from the signed `storeIds`/`stores` mapping. The provider independently admits only exact active tenant-summary IDs; any embedded or freshly read store must carry coherent exact store/tenant aliases equal to the signed scope and must not be inactive, deleted, auth-disabled or blocked. A contradictory, inaccessible, foreign or stale context leaves the base/login session unchanged and is removed from local storage.
5. **Transformation order:** The raw MenuList session is first projected to the authorized active store. Only then may the route/host project an Answerlattice product account. This prevents a valid MenuList context from being compared against and cleared by already-projected sister-product aliases.
6. **Caching/concurrency:** The browser caches only the raw session for five seconds and deduplicates only the raw fetch promise. Cache hits, request creators and callers joining an in-flight request each apply the current pathname/hostname scope independently, so a route transition cannot inherit the first caller's product selection.
7. **Side effects/cache:** The only mutation is removal or exact rewrite of the browser-local active-store hint. No Firestore, Firebase Auth, Redux, SWR, public cache, route cache or publication write occurs. Product/store projection returns copied session objects and never mutates the raw cached object.
8. **Errors/observability:** Oversized/malformed session responses and request failures follow bounded auth diagnostics. Unavailable local storage is tolerated. Invalid browser context fails closed to the signed base session rather than creating an owner-visible auth failure.
9. **Consumers/output:** Owner DAL and React hook consumers both run the same runtime projector followed by the same selected-store and current route/host product projection. Eligible Answerlattice support routes therefore cannot retain MenuList scope, and selected-outlet hook consumers cannot retain the login store. The projected session remains private browser state and is not a persistence or server-authorization source; protected operations must still re-establish current server authority.
10. **Tests/external:** Store-switch behavior covers valid mapping, forged store, contradictory tenant and malformed numeric values. Serialized-session behavior covers ISO versus `Date`, scientific IDs, top/nested identity/scope disagreement, duplicate-role conflict, product-account admission, explicit onboarding nulls and hook-source parity. Active-session behavior covers product projection immutability and source-level ordering/raw-request dedupe invariants. Auth security matrix, tenant-safety, Answerlattice runtime aggregate, TypeScript and lint gates pass. Authenticated multi-tab route-transition and persisted legacy-storage browser smoke require a deployed app and remain external.

**Reverse trace:** `activeStoreContext` has owner UI writers and this single reviewed reader/projection boundary. `/api/auth/session` is cached only as raw signed-session data; every effective store/product consumer receives a fresh projection. No browser value can add tenant/store membership or change server-side claims.

### DF-AL-ACCESS-CONTEXT-001 — Signed Answerlattice scope to current browser management authority

1. **Trigger/entry:** The client-only `AnswerlatticeAccessProvider` runs when its signed session identity or pathname changes and on explicit `refresh()`. It sends `GET /api/answerlattice/access` with same-origin credentials, no-store cache policy and manual redirect handling.
2. **Authentication/authorization:** `withAuth()` establishes the current signed session before the route reads data. The default-enabled staff-access feature flag is checked before access preparation. `getAnswerlatticeAccessContext()` independently resolves exact Answerlattice product, tenant and store scope and returns no context when current membership, store, user, role or lifecycle truth is invalid.
3. **Tenant/store derivation:** The server derives tenant/store only from `resolveAnswerlatticeSessionScope(session)`, never from browser headers, query strings or request bodies. The provider's request identity includes signed user ID, tenant, store, role and session expiry so a workspace/session transition reloads even while NextAuth remains `authenticated`.
4. **Raw input/runtime boundary:** The request has no body. The private JSON response is capped at 64 KiB and must contain an exact access object: booleans retain boolean kinds, IDs are finite positive numbers, roles remain an array, permissions are boolean-only, and user/store strings are present. Rejected or malformed responses never become access state.
5. **Reads/transformation:** The access builder performs one exact `stores/{sId}` read plus a bounded user lookup, validates product/scope aliases, normalizes registered role permissions and projects only current user identity, store name, roles, permission booleans and management/platform flags. Raw store/user documents are not serialized.
6. **Writes/cache/queues:** No Firestore, Auth, Storage, Redux, SWR, local-storage, server-cache, public-cache, queue or webhook write occurs. Response headers are private no-store; browser state is process-memory React context only.
7. **Concurrency/idempotency:** Every load claims a monotonic request ID. A newer request and effect cleanup invalidate every older completion; stale success, failure and `finally` branches cannot overwrite current access, error or loading state. Repeated current requests are read-only and converge on the latest response.
8. **Errors/observability:** Parse, rejected-response and invalid-response failures emit bounded runtime diagnostics containing only response status/OK state. Owner-visible errors are fixed text plus a bounded server code. Stale failures are ignored after invalidation and cannot erase newer valid access.
9. **Consumers/tests:** Dashboard, sidebar and access hooks consume the current React context; protected mutations still repeat server authorization and do not trust the browser projection. The latest-request behavior suite proves newer-request and cleanup invalidation, while staff/access contracts and the central runtime verifier pin exact scope/response behavior.
10. **Unresolved/external:** Authenticated two-workspace rapid-switch contention and deployed browser behavior require the normal app release path and were not run because Vercel deployment is opt-in.

**Reverse trace:** `/api/answerlattice/access` is the only producer of this provider's `AnswerlatticeAccessContext`. Store/user documents are server-read authorities; the response is a private allowlisted projection. Provider state has no persistence writer, and session identity plus latest-request settlement prevents a prior tenant/store response from becoming the current consumer value.
