### AUDIT-AUTH-CLAIM-IDENTITY-001 — Claim links could select an arbitrary duplicate business or remain valid without expiry

- **Finding ID:** AUDIT-AUTH-CLAIM-IDENTITY-001
- **Severity:** P0
- **Status:** Closed in source; legacy duplicate/missing-expiry inventory requires authorized live-data access
- **File and exact line/function:** `getUniqueMessagingUserByClaimToken()` and `assertMessagingUserClaimIsAvailable()` in `src/lib/auth/claimAccountConcurrency.ts`; public `/api/auth/claim-account` and `/api/auth/validate-claim` lookup/admission paths
- **Flow ID:** DF-AUTH-CLAIM-001
- **Affected data structure:** Bearer `users.claimToken`, required `claimTokenExpiresAt`, claim owner/store mapping and public claim-preview DTO
- **Producer:** Messaging onboarding publish transaction mints 32 random bytes and a seven-day Firestore Timestamp expiry.
- **Consumer:** Public personalized claim preview and Google/email/password/WhatsApp account ownership transfer.
- **Trigger:** Two user documents persist the same claim token, or a legacy token document has missing/malformed expiry.
- **Observed behavior:** Both routes used `.limit(1)` and selected an arbitrary business when identity was ambiguous. Account-claim admission treated missing expiry as valid indefinitely. Preview independently admitted missing/malformed expiry and trusted legacy `name`/`phone` runtime types; its expired-token update could clear a concurrently replaced token.
- **Expected behavior:** A bearer token maps to exactly one eligible messaging owner, always has a parseable future expiry, and preview enforces the same state/scope/owner contract as final claim. Cleanup must not erase newer truth.
- **Root cause:** Cryptographic producer uniqueness and a superseded historical no-expiry decision were assumed to guarantee persisted legacy uniqueness/expiry; public preview duplicated weaker validation and cleanup logic.
- **Security/tenant impact:** Highest severity arbitrary cross-tenant business selection/ownership risk under duplicate token data, plus indefinite bearer-link exposure for missing-expiry legacy rows.
- **Data-integrity impact:** A wrong messaging user could be reserved and transferred; unconditional preview cleanup could erase a replacement token.
- **Public-truth impact:** Successful wrong-business claim could later mutate another tenant's public business truth. Preview could disclose another business name and masked phone suffix.
- **Cache impact:** Successful claim still uses the existing public menu/OBP/store/client-store invalidation path; no cache key changed.
- **Backward-compatibility impact:** Unique unexpired active owner tokens retain all three modes. Ambiguous or missing/malformed-expiry legacy rows now require operator remediation instead of guessing or remaining indefinite.
- **Fix:** Centralize exact token lookup with `.limit(2)` and ambiguity refusal; require future expiry in the shared claimability guard; make preview reuse the same eligibility contract; conditionally clear expired tokens in a re-reading transaction; normalize bounded preview strings; label the old no-expiry document as superseded.
- **Files changed:** Claim concurrency helper, claim-account route, validate-claim route, emulator, auth verifier, auth docs, production audit, changelog and deep-audit/review-state evidence.
- **Regression test:** Claim-account Firestore emulator covers duplicate/unique identity, missing/malformed expiry, active reservation, finalization, rollback and compensation boundaries.
- **Validation commands/result:** `npm run test:claim-account-concurrency:emulator`, `npm run verify:auth-security-failure-matrix`, root TypeScript and `git diff --check` exited 0.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** Restart 84 P0 focused closure; clean counter remains zero and complete security/data-flow restart required.

### AUDIT-AUTH-STATUS-001 — Access-status allowed stale or mismatched tenant/store references

- **Finding ID:** AUDIT-AUTH-STATUS-001
- **Severity:** P1
- **Status:** Closed in source/tests; authenticated hosted browser/live deleted-scope proof pending
- **File and exact line/function:** `GET()`, `getEntityData()`, `isPlatformAccessSession()` and `isStoreOwnedByTenant()` in `src/app/api/auth/access-status/route.ts`; `getAccessEndedCopy()` in `src/components/auth/SessionExpiryMonitor.tsx`
- **Flow ID:** DF-AUTH-STATUS-001
- **Affected data structure:** `/api/auth/access-status` response `{valid, reason, checkedAt}`, `users.tenantId/storeId`, session `tId/sId`, `tenants/{tenantId}`, `stores/{storeId}.tenantId/tId`
- **Producer:** Authenticated NextAuth session plus current Admin SDK reads of user, tenant and store documents.
- **Consumer:** `SessionExpiryMonitor`, owner desktop/mobile shell sessions, NextAuth/Firebase access refresh behavior and downstream owner mutations that depend on an active session remaining valid.
- **Trigger:** A non-platform session references a deleted/missing tenant document, a deleted/missing store document, an existing store without a checked tenant document, or a store document whose persisted tenant reference no longer matches the checked tenant.
- **Observed behavior:** Missing tenant/store documents were represented as `data: null` and therefore passed the blocked-entity check. A non-platform store-scoped session could also pass without any tenant document checked. Store ownership was not compared to the tenant being checked. The route could return `{valid: true}` for stale, omitted-tenant, or incoherent session scope.
- **Expected behavior:** Non-platform sessions with explicit tenant/store references must fail closed when the referenced document is missing, a store-scoped session must not remain valid without checked tenant context, and a referenced store must belong to the same normalized tenant document before the session remains valid. Platform sessions may retain absent platform-scope tolerance but still honor blocked referenced entities.
- **Root cause:** The route validated document-ID syntax and blocked flags but treated absent referenced documents as a harmless no-block state, allowed a store-scoped success without tenant context, and had no store-to-tenant coherence check.
- **Security/tenant impact:** A stale or incoherent owner session could remain active after tenant/store deletion or data corruption. This is an authorization-boundary defect, though no tenant/store document fields were serialized by this endpoint.
- **Data-integrity impact:** Owner UI could keep submitting requests under a session whose tenant/store authority should already have ended.
- **Public-truth impact:** Downstream owner mutations could attempt to update or publish under stale scope until later route-specific guards rejected them.
- **Cache impact:** No server/public cache writes occur in this route. Browser session/local state could remain active until the poll detected another access-ended reason; the repair terminates those stale states earlier.
- **Backward-compatibility impact:** Valid non-platform sessions are unchanged. New owner/staff onboarding sessions without tenant/store references remain admitted because absent references are distinct from missing referenced documents. Platform sessions retain explicit tolerance for absent platform tenant/store scope.
- **Fix:** Preserve document IDs from `getEntityData()`, fail non-platform explicit tenant/store references as `TENANT_NOT_FOUND` or `STORE_NOT_FOUND` when missing, fail a non-platform existing-store session when no tenant document was checked, add a platform-role tolerance helper, normalize `stores.tenantId ?? stores.tId` and compare it to the checked tenant document ID before returning `valid: true`, and map the new reasons to the owner-safe access-ended modal.
- **Files changed:** `src/app/api/auth/access-status/route.ts`, `src/components/auth/SessionExpiryMonitor.tsx`, `scripts/verification/verify-auth-security-failure-matrix.js`, `scripts/verification/verify-menulist-api-tenant-safety.js`, `__docs__/auth/auth_firebase.md`, `__docs__/auth/auth_mobile-support.md`, `__docs__/audits/menulist-production-readiness-audit.md`, `__docs__/changelog.md`, and deep-audit artifacts.
- **Regression test:** Static source gates now require `TENANT_NOT_FOUND`, `STORE_NOT_FOUND`, `STORE_TENANT_MISMATCH`, explicit platform tolerance, omitted-tenant/store-scoped fail-closed handling, normalized store-tenant comparison, browser reason mapping and docs/changelog evidence.
- **Validation commands/result:** `npm run verify:auth-security-failure-matrix` and `npm run verify:menulist-api-tenant-safety` exited 0 before artifact regeneration; final Restart 120 gate bundle records post-artifact TypeScript, lint, docs, audit-tool and diff results.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** Restart 120 auth/session-status tenant-store coherence closure; clean counter reset to zero.

- **Affected structure/producer/consumer/trigger:** Private access-status `{valid,reason}` response produced for one signed NextAuth session and consumed by the global browser monitor. The account/workspace changes while the old request is in flight, or a focus/interval check overlaps a session transition.
- **Observed/expected/root cause:** One unscoped boolean represented all in-flight checks. Cleanup removed timers but did not invalidate the response, and the end-access effect did not prove it still belonged to the current session. A delayed 401/403/`valid:false` response could therefore display old-account state and call `signOutSession()` after a different session became current. Only the latest request for the exact current session may end browser access.
- **Security/tenant impact:** A prior tenant/account decision could terminate the current account's session and display the wrong access-ended state. This is a cross-session authorization-side-effect race and P0 availability/security defect; no protected route authorization was bypassed.
- **Data/public/cache impact:** No Firestore/public truth is mutated. The effect changes private browser modal/local-storage/session state and can force navigation/sign-out under the wrong session.
- **Backward compatibility/migration:** No stored schema or migration. Valid current-session 401/403/revocation behavior, polling cadence, response contract and owner copy remain unchanged.
- **Fix/files changed:** Moved the monotonic request primitive to shared runtime scope; bound polling to exact user/tenant/store/product/role/expiry identity; made every access-ended call carry the current request ID; invalidated in-flight work on session/effect cleanup; and reset modal/reason state when exact authenticated identity changes. Updated auth and Answerlattice source gates plus auth implementation/Firebase/production-readiness/changelog/audit evidence.
- **Regression test:** `npm run test:latest-request-guard` proves a superseded request and cleanup-invalidated request cannot settle; the auth/security verifier pins identity binding, request claims, current checks, request-bound sign-out and removal of the unscoped boolean.
- **Validation commands/result:** `npm run test:latest-request-guard`, `npm run verify:auth-security-failure-matrix`, `node scripts/verification/verify-answerlattice-runtime-truth.js`, exact root TypeScript and focused ESLint exit 0. Docs/audit artifact/diff gates are recorded in the Restart 541 ledger after regeneration.
- **Re-audit pass:** Restart 541 closure; tenant/auth/client-state clean counters reset to zero.

### AUDIT-AL-KB-DELETE-001 — Job deletion could erase published article provenance

- **Severity:** P1

- **Flow ID:** DF-AL-KB-001
- **Affected data structure:** `kb_generation_jobs`, related `kb_articles.jobId`, review navigation and published history
- **Producer:** Platform job-history/active-card delete action
- **Consumer:** Published article provenance, help-center operators and later audit/reconciliation tooling
- **Trigger:** A platform administrator deletes a published history job or a job whose related articles are published/active.
- **Observed behavior:** The job could be removed while published articles were preserved, leaving their `jobId` lineage dangling; the history UI exposed deletion for published rows.
- **Expected behavior:** Published/active article provenance must remain durable. Only unpublished safe terminal/review states may be deleted, with the DAL authoritative over UI affordances.

- **Backward-compatibility impact:** Existing published jobs remain visible; safe unpublished cleanup remains available.

### AUDIT-AL-KB-CLEANUP-001 — Storage cleanup failures were acknowledged as successful deletion

- **Finding ID:** AUDIT-AL-KB-CLEANUP-001
- **Severity:** P1
- **Status:** Closed locally; live Storage proof remains external
- **File and exact line/function:** `src/database/kb-generation/jobs.ts` `deleteIngestionJob()` Storage result handling and operation ordering
- **Flow ID:** DF-AL-KB-001
- **Affected data structure:** Source-file Storage objects, `kb_generation_jobs.deletionRun` and deletion acknowledgement DTO
- **Producer:** `deleteFileByUrl()` fulfilled `{ success: false }` cleanup results
- **Consumer:** Platform delete success UI, retention/audit operators and retry behavior
- **Trigger:** Firebase Storage deletion returns an acknowledged failure rather than rejecting its promise.
- **Observed behavior:** `Promise.allSettled()` counted only rejected promises, so fulfilled failures counted as zero. The job had already been deleted, preventing a reliable retry while private source files could remain.
- **Expected behavior:** Every Storage result must explicitly acknowledge success; any failure must retain an observable, leased, retryable job record and must not return deletion success. Restart 315 supersedes persisted source deletion entirely because one job cannot establish workspace-wide non-reference; immediate cleanup remains limited to attempt-owned uploads before persistence.
- **Root cause:** Promise settlement was confused with operation success and destructive Firestore writes occurred before recoverable external cleanup completed.
- **Security/tenant impact:** Source files can contain private customer/business material; silent retention is a data-lifecycle risk.
- **Data-integrity impact:** Firestore claimed deletion while Storage truth diverged, with no durable retry owner.
- **Public-truth impact:** None directly; source and review artifacts are private.
- **Cache impact:** None.
- **Backward-compatibility impact:** Successful deletion is unchanged except for an extra lease/finalization write; failed cleanup now produces retry copy and retained state.
- **Fix:** The original repair claimed a transaction-owned deletion lease, inspected explicit Storage acknowledgements and retained failed cleanup state. Restart 315 preserves the lease, atomic draft deletion and final ownership check but retains persisted source objects with a bounded diagnostic, eliminating the unsafe one-job Storage delete and its now-retired result-counting boundary.
- **Files changed:** Generation-job DAL, pure deletion boundary, behavioral test, type mirrors, publish guard, runtime verifier, docs/changelog and audit evidence.
- **Regression test:** `test-answerlattice-ingestion-job-deletion-boundary.ts` pins safe statuses/product/timestamp/query admission; the runtime verifier pins lease/ownership ordering, deferred source cleanup and absence of direct persisted-source deletion.
- **Validation commands/result:** Dedicated behavioral test, runtime source gate, exact TypeScript and scoped ESLint exit 0; live workspace reference inventory remains external.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** Restart 85 P1 focused closure, superseded by the safer Restart 315 shared-reference lifecycle; clean counter remains zero.

### AUDIT-AL-KB-SOURCE-SHARED-REFERENCE-001 — Deleting one ingestion job could remove source media retained by another job

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-AL-KB-SOURCE-SHARED-REFERENCE-001 / P1 / Closed locally in restart 315.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/database/kb-generation/jobs.ts::addIngestionJob/deleteIngestionJob`, `UploadModal.tsx`, DF-AL-KB-001; attempt upload or existing workspace path -> `kb_generation_jobs.sourceFiles[]` -> draft/review/publish consumers -> safe job deletion -> Answerlattice Storage.

A second job can therefore persist the same source object. Deleting either safe unpublished job deleted every listed object before deleting the job, breaking the surviving job's retry, review, audit or generation input. The path-prefix check proved tenant scope, not exclusive lifecycle ownership.
- **Expected/security/data/public/cache/compatibility:** Job deletion may delete exact-scope draft articles and the selected job under its existing lease, but persisted source reclamation requires a bounded workspace-wide job/reference inventory. Published provenance refusal, DTO shape, job idempotency, public cache and legacy source-path compatibility remain unchanged.
- **Fix/files/cost:** `deleteIngestionJob()` deduplicates source paths only for a bounded `answerlattice_kb_source_cleanup_deferred_shared_reference` diagnostic, performs no Storage delete, and returns the existing truthful `storageCleanupFailedCount: 0`. The unused cleanup-result helper/test assertions were removed. KB spec/implementation/Firebase/forensic docs now describe zero Storage deletes and workspace-wide reclamation authority. Existing failed upload-to-job handoff still cleans newly uploaded attempt objects before persistence. Normal deletion removes N Storage deletes; Firestore reads/writes remain `3+N`/`2+N`.
- **Regression/validation/closure:** The runtime verifier requires the diagnostic and rejects direct mapping of persisted job sources into `deleteFileByUrl()`. The focused deletion contract, runtime gate, exact root TypeScript, scoped ESLint and `git diff --check` pass. Authenticated shared-path multi-job execution and historical bucket/reference inventory remain external; no Firebase infrastructure changed and the clean counter is zero.

### AUDIT-AI-PROMPT-CACHE-CLEANUP-RACE-001 — Expiry cleanup could delete a concurrently refreshed prompt cache

- **Finding ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-AI-PROMPT-CACHE-CLEANUP-RACE-001 / P1 / Closed locally in restart 316; scoped QA Function deployment required.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/lib/ai/imageGenerationPromptCache.ts::writeImagePromptCacheSource/copyCachedImagePromptToStore`, `src/lib/ai/imagePromptCacheBoundary.ts`, `functions/src/schedulers/menulistMaintenanceScheduler.ts::runImagePromptCacheCleanup`, `functions/src/schedulers/imagePromptCacheRetentionBoundary.ts`, DF-AI-IMAGE-001; normalized prompt/config -> cache key -> prepared private source -> cache doc -> store-owned copy -> expiry scheduler.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed/root cause:** Every write for one cache key overwrote deterministic `system/aiImagePromptCache/v1/{cacheKey}.{ext}` bytes and merged the same document. Cleanup queried an expired snapshot, deleted that path, and batch-deleted the snapshot row without re-reading. If a writer refreshed between query and deletion, cleanup could delete the writer's new bytes and refreshed document. The root cause was mutable object identity plus stale-snapshot deletion across Firestore and Storage, which cannot commit atomically.
- **Expected/security/data/public/cache/compatibility:** Every refresh owns an immutable source version. The active row changes transactionally. Cleanup may delete only an exact cache-key path and may delete the row only when current `sourcePath` and `expiresAt` still equal expired truth. Cache hits must continue copying bytes into the requesting tenant/store path; raw prompt text remains absent. Legacy v1 rows remain cleanup-admissible, while current cache keys intentionally advance to v2.
- **Fix/files/cost:** Cache key/path version advances to 2 and sources use `system/aiImagePromptCache/v2/{cacheKey}/{sourceVersion}.{ext}`. Writer replacement is one Firestore transaction read/write, returns the exact previous source, and best-effort deletes only that exact-key prior version. Scheduler deletion keeps the capped expired query and one Storage delete, then adds one transaction read and conditional document delete per candidate. Pure boundaries validate exact paths and current source/expiry equality. No collection, index, rule, owner setting, provider call or public cache behavior changed.
- **Failure/idempotency/observability:** Concurrent writers serialize on the cache row and cannot overwrite one another's bytes. A stale scheduler can delete only its immutable claimed source; if current truth changed, the current row remains. Invalid/malformed paths are skipped, cleanup errors retain the row for retry, and stable bounded diagnostics disclose superseded-source or finalization failures without prompts, keys, URLs or raw provider payloads. An unresolvable upload-to-transaction acknowledgement may retain an unreferenced immutable version rather than risking deletion of committed truth; bounded historical object inventory remains required for that residual lifecycle.
- **Regression/validation/closure:** `test:image-prompt-cache-boundary` proves versioned exact-key source admission and media validation. `test:image-prompt-cache-retention-boundary` proves stale-source, refreshed-expiry and malformed-expiry refusal. `verify:ai-accounting`, Functions build/lint/preflight, exact root TypeScript, scoped ESLint and `git diff --check` pass after repairing one strict undefined guard and one stale verifier-location assertion. The scoped QA deploy completed predeploy lint/build, then Cloud Resource Manager returned HTTP 403 before upload; emulator/provider concurrency injection and deployed scheduler proof remain pending, and the clean counter is zero.

### AUDIT-AL-KB-ARTICLE-SCOPE-001 — Article bulk mutations derived ownership from session rather than stored rows

- **Finding ID:** AUDIT-AL-KB-ARTICLE-SCOPE-001
- **Severity:** P0
- **Status:** Closed locally; authenticated contention/deployment proof remains external
- **File and exact line/function:** `src/database/knowledgeBase/articles.ts` readable filters/final guards, `addArticle()`, `updateArticle()`, `deleteArticle()` and `bulkUpdateArticleStatus()`
- **Flow ID:** DF-AL-KB-ARTICLE-001
- **Affected data structure:** `kb_articles.pId/tId/sId`, article status/active state and KB cache-version scope
- **Producer:** Answerlattice owner/platform knowledge-base UI and generation review UI
- **Consumer:** Hosted Help, widget/RAG retrieval, categories, FAQ links, embeddings and public cache versions
- **Trigger:** A platform selection spans workspaces, a stale/malformed article carries a different product/scope, or a caller supplies an arbitrary ID/scope.
- **Observed behavior:** Bulk status composed tenant/store from the current session and updated arbitrary unbounded IDs without reading stored ownership. Several readers omitted `pId: AL` or final product/scope checks, and single writes could merge caller/session scope into an existing row.
- **Expected behavior:** Every read and mutation must admit exact Answerlattice product/workspace identity; mutations must derive ownership from stored rows and recheck it transactionally. Bulk work must be exact, bounded, one-workspace and status-allowlisted.
- **Root cause:** Shared composer/session convenience was treated as authoritative entity ownership, while the globally authorized platform surface made mixed-workspace selection possible.
- **Security/tenant impact:** A platform/global workflow could corrupt another workspace's article ownership or expose cross-product rows; highest-severity tenant/product isolation defect.
- **Data-integrity impact:** Article tenant/store fields, status, cache invalidation and downstream linkage could diverge.
- **Public-truth impact:** Wrong-workspace publish/archive or stale cache scope could change the wrong Help/widget output.
- **Cache impact:** Previous bulk writes bumped/revalidated session scope rather than stored article scope.
- **Backward-compatibility impact:** Valid single-workspace owner/platform actions remain; malformed IDs, mixed scopes, unsupported statuses and non-AL rows now fail closed.
- **Fix:** Require `pId: AL` in queries/final guards, normalize all document IDs, derive single mutation scope from stored articles, recheck it in transactions, cap bulk updates at 100 unique IDs, allow only publish/archive and remove unused unsafe bulk deletion.
- **Files changed:** Article DAL, pure article mutation boundary/test, runtime verifier, Help/KB/FAQ docs, changelog and audit evidence.
- **Regression test:** `test-answerlattice-article-mutation-boundary.ts` covers exact IDs/status/product/scope and mixed-workspace refusal; runtime verifier pins transaction ownership.
- **Validation commands/result:** Dedicated behavioral test, Answerlattice runtime suite and root TypeScript passed; aggregate restart pending.
- **Re-audit pass in which confirmed closed:** Restart 86 P0 focused closure; complete tenant/publication restart required.

### AUDIT-AL-KB-FAQ-ATOMIC-001 — Article and linked FAQ public truth changed in split best-effort writes

- **Finding ID:** AUDIT-AL-KB-FAQ-ATOMIC-001
- **Severity:** P1
- **Status:** Closed locally; emulator/authenticated contention proof pending
- **File and exact line/function:** `src/database/knowledgeBase/articles.ts` article update/delete and `src/database/answerlattice/faqs.ts` FAQ save/archive
- **Flow ID:** DF-AL-KB-ARTICLE-001, DF-AL-FAQ-001

- **Producer:** Article editor/delete, FAQ management save/archive
- **Consumer:** Public FAQ tabs, Help Center, widget contextual answers and product-surface summaries
- **Trigger:** Article content changes/deletes while linked FAQ maintenance fails or races; FAQ save links a missing/cross-workspace article.
- **Observed behavior:** Article success returned before fire-and-forget FAQ review/archive. FAQ save used `batch.set(..., merge)` on linked article refs without verifying existence/scope, so platform authority could create skeletal article documents. Split writes could leave published FAQs answering from changed/deleted truth.
- **Expected behavior:** FAQ relationship mirrors and public status transitions must serialize with their article and cannot create missing entities.
- **Root cause:** Relationship maintenance was modeled as non-blocking cache hygiene rather than coupled public truth.
- **Security/tenant impact:** Stored FAQ/article scope is now independently rechecked; cross-workspace links fail before writes.
- **Data-integrity impact:** Prevents dangling links, skeletal articles and mismatched `faqIds` mirrors.

- **Cache impact:** Article changes revalidate FAQ/KB/context tags only after the coupled transaction; existing cache versioning remains.
- **Backward-compatibility impact:** Valid owner behavior remains; inconsistent legacy links fail closed instead of being silently overwritten.
- **Fix:** Serialize FAQ save/archive with stored FAQ and previous/next article reads; use transaction `update` for existing mirrors. Article update/delete queries a capped linked set, unions the current mirror, validates every row and changes FAQ status in the same transaction as the article mutation. Retired split helpers were removed.
- **Files changed:** Article DAL, FAQ DAL, runtime verifier, FAQ/KB/Help docs, changelog and audit evidence.
- **Regression test:** Runtime verifier pins missing-link refusal, no skeletal `batch.set`, article transaction FAQ transitions and retired split helpers; behavioral scope test covers exact product/workspace.

### AUDIT-AL-MCP-TOKEN-001 — MCP session verification trusted an unchecked decoded JSON cast

- **Finding ID:** AUDIT-AL-MCP-TOKEN-001
- **Severity:** P1
- **Status:** Closed
- **File and exact line/function:** `src/lib/answerlattice/mcpSession.ts` `verifyAnswerlatticeMcpSessionToken()`
- **Flow ID:** DF-AL-MCP-001
- **Affected data structure:** Signed MCP session token payload and scope claims
- **Producer:** Base64url token payload/signature
- **Consumer:** Answerlattice MCP context/signal route
- **Trigger:** A signed token contained coercible string IDs, unknown/duplicate scopes, unexpected fields, invalid versions/timestamps, excessive lifetime, or an extra third token segment.
- **Observed behavior:** Decoded JSON was cast directly to the TypeScript interface, IDs were checked through `Number()`, scope/version/time shapes were not validated, and `split('.')` ignored additional segments.
- **Expected behavior:** The issuer must refuse invalid claims before signing, and signature verification must be followed by an exact runtime payload contract and exact two-segment token framing.
- **Root cause:** Compile-time token types were treated as runtime proof after JSON decoding.
- **Security/tenant impact:** Prevents malformed scope and capability claims from entering MCP authorization even if a signer/caller produces an invalid payload.

- **Cache impact:** Invalid bundle-version claims cannot affect MCP bundle selection.
- **Backward-compatibility impact:** Tokens produced by the maintained issuer are unchanged; malformed legacy/custom tokens now reject.
- **Fix:** Add an exact-key payload parser used both before signing and after verification, numeric safe-integer scope/version/time validation, scope allowlist/uniqueness, 900-second lifetime bound and exact two-segment framing.
- **Files changed:** MCP session helper, focused behavioral test, package/runtime suite registry, runtime verifier, changelog and audit evidence.
- **Regression test:** Valid round-trip plus issuer-side unsupported scope and verifier-side extra segment, string tenant, unknown/duplicate scope, excessive lifetime and unexpected-field cases.

### AUDIT-ANALYTICS-023 — Browser analytics state and queue could lose data or retry permanently

- **Finding ID / severity / status:** AUDIT-ANALYTICS-023 / P1 / Closed locally.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/lib/analytics/unified.ts` session milestone/source/filter reads; `src/database/analytics/index.ts` queue restore/enqueue/flush/retry; `src/lib/analytics/browserState.ts`; `src/lib/analytics/queueBoundary.ts`; browser event -> session state -> local queue -> public route.
- **Observed / expected / root cause:** Parsed `sessionStorage` objects were trusted as typed state, persisted queue tuples trusted caller keys/scope/counters, flush success deleted the complete queue entry even when events arrived during the request, and every HTTP/network failure retried every 30 seconds without an attempt/age limit. Session state was also committed after a rejected enqueue. Browser persistence is untrusted and a flush must drain only what it actually sent.
- **Impact:** Malformed local state could throw and suppress customer analytics; forged or stale queue entries could create repeated network/route work; permanent 4xx failures could loop across reloads; and valid counters merged during an active request could be lost.
- **Fix / invariants:** Added exact bounded browser-state and persisted-queue normalizers; canonical tenant/store/project/date re-keying; duplicate/future/stale/over-wide/oversized rejection; 20-scope, 12-retry, 48-hour, and 512K storage caps; retry classification with bounded backoff; in-flight snapshot subtraction; and milestone persistence only after queue admission. Valid traffic retains one coalesced Admin write per flush.
- **Regression / validation:** `test-analytics-browser-boundary.ts` covers malformed state, forged keys, invalid scope/date/count/retry, duplicate amplification, queue width/capacity, additive merge, and in-flight snapshot drain. `npm run verify:analytics-write-boundary`, `npm run test:analytics:rules`, focused lint, root TypeScript, and diff integrity pass.
- **Residual:** Delivery remains intentionally at-least-once. A network failure after the server commits but before the browser receives the response can still duplicate aggregate increments; eliminating that would require a durable idempotency receipt and additional Firebase cost.
- **Re-audit pass:** Restart 175 browser state/queue success-failure-concurrency retrace; clean counter reset.

### AUDIT-FIRESTORE-SANITIZER-MIRROR-001 — Isolated Functions sanitizers drifted from the authoritative Firestore value contract

- **Finding ID / severity / status:** AUDIT-FIRESTORE-SANITIZER-MIRROR-001 / P3 / Closed locally; QA deployment evidence pending the combined scoped Functions attempt.
- **File and exact line/function:** `functions/src/lib/sanitizeForFirestore.ts::sanitizeForFirestore()` / `sanitizeValue()`; `functions-answerlattice/src/lib/sanitizeForFirestore.ts::sanitizeForFirestore()` / `sanitizeValue()`; authoritative comparison at `src/lib/firestore/sanitizeForFirestore.ts`; regression at `scripts/verification/test-request-body-composition-boundary.ts`.
- **Flow ID:** DF-FIRESTORE-SANITIZE-MIRROR-001; DF-MENULIST-FUNCTION-WRITE-001; DF-ANSWERLATTICE-FUNCTION-WRITE-001.
- **Affected data structure:** MenuList and Answerlattice Cloud Functions Firestore write payloads containing Date values, SDK atomic objects, timestamp-like compatibility values, undefined fields, arrays, and legacy unsafe object keys.
- **Producer / consumer / trigger:** Functions DALs and job writers produce sanitized Firestore payloads; Firestore Admin consumes them; the trigger was a cross-runtime reverse trace from the authoritative sanitizer contract to both isolated package mirrors.
- **Observed behavior:** The root contract supported a discriminated path-aware atomic transform and an explicit unsafe-key omission mode, but both Functions mirrors exposed only Date conversion and undefined omission, always rejected unsafe keys, duplicated path interpolation, and claimed an unchanged generic return even when top-level `undefined` becomes `null`.
- **Expected behavior:** Isolated package mirrors must implement the same documented options, default rejection behavior, path semantics, SDK-value preservation, and return contract as the root sanitizer so callers do not receive runtime-specific Firestore shapes.
- **Root cause:** The root sanitizer evolved after the Functions copies were introduced, with no regression exercising the newer options against every runtime implementation.
- **Security/tenant impact:** No tenant-isolation bypass was found. Reject remains the default for prototype-pollution keys; omission occurs only when an internal caller explicitly selects compatibility mode.
- **Data-integrity impact:** A Functions caller using the authoritative atomic-transform contract would silently preserve a timestamp-like custom object instead of converting it, and a legacy compatibility reader could not request safe omission consistently across runtimes.
- **Public-truth impact:** No current public-truth writer was found using the missing options; this was a concrete cross-runtime contract risk rather than an observed persisted public-output mismatch.
- **Cache impact:** None.
- **Backward-compatibility impact:** Existing Date conversion, undefined omission/null behavior, cycle/accessor/array checks, SDK atomic-object preservation, and reject-by-default unsafe-key behavior are unchanged. The new modes are opt-in.
- **Fix:** Added the discriminated `atomicTransform(value, path)` hook before non-plain SDK preservation, explicit `unsafeObjectKey: 'reject' | 'omit'`, shared child-path construction, and the undefined-aware conditional return type to both Functions mirrors.
- **Files changed:** `functions/src/lib/sanitizeForFirestore.ts`; `functions-answerlattice/src/lib/sanitizeForFirestore.ts`; `scripts/verification/test-request-body-composition-boundary.ts`; audit artifacts.
- **Regression test:** The request-body composition boundary now invokes atomic conversion/path propagation and unsafe-key omission against the root sanitizer and both Functions mirrors while retaining undefined, Date, SDK sentinel, and cycle cases.
- **Validation commands:** `npm run test:request-body-composition-boundary`; `npm run verify:async-data-flow-boundaries`; `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false`; `npm --prefix functions run build`; `npm --prefix functions-answerlattice run build`; `npx eslint functions/src/lib/sanitizeForFirestore.ts functions-answerlattice/src/lib/sanitizeForFirestore.ts scripts/verification/test-request-body-composition-boundary.ts`.
- **Validation result:** All listed local commands passed. Firebase QA deployment is intentionally deferred until the concurrent bounded Functions audits settle, then both affected packages will receive one exact-current deploy attempt.
- **Re-audit pass:** Restart 182 cross-runtime Firestore sanitizer contract trace; clean counter reset.

### AUDIT-OWNER-BUSINESS-HEALTH-WRITE-001 — Authoritative Business Health rebuilds retained stale optional fields

- **Finding ID / severity / status:** AUDIT-OWNER-BUSINESS-HEALTH-WRITE-001 / P2 / Runtime fix and focused regression closed locally; exact-current Functions build and QA deployment evidence pending.
- **File and exact line/function:** `functions/src/ownerBusinessAssistant/ownerBusinessHealthWriters.ts::writeOwnerBusinessHealthDocs()`; regression in `scripts/verification/verify-owner-business-assistant-hardening.ts::verifyOwnerBusinessHealthWriteReplacementSemantics()`; consumers in `src/lib/ownerBusinessAssistant/server/buildOwnerBusinessAssistantContextPacket.ts` and protected Business Health current/analytics routes.
- **Flow ID:** DF-OWNER-BUSINESS-HEALTH-BUILD-001; DF-OWNER-BUSINESS-HEALTH-READ-001; DF-OWNER-BUSINESS-HEALTH-CACHE-001.
- **Affected data structure:** `platformSummary/ownerBusinessHealthCurrent_{tId}_{sId}`, `ownerBusinessHealthSnapshot_{tId}_{sId}_{localDate}`, `ownerBusinessAnalyticsIndex_{tId}_{sId}`, and the intentionally partial `ownerBusinessHealthMultiLocation_{tId}.stores.{sId}` map.
- **Producer / consumer / trigger:** The consolidated store intelligence scheduler produces complete health/analytics read models; protected owner APIs and context-packet caches consume them; the trigger was a reverse trace from sanitizer omission semantics through each Firestore `batch.set()` mode.
- **Observed behavior:** The writer omitted undefined values and then used `{ merge: true }` for complete current, same-day snapshot, and analytics-index documents. If a later run removed `analyticsTeaser`, a top item, a period, a project summary, a source field, or a legacy property, Firestore retained the older value and the post-write cache invalidation merely caused the stale merged document to be read and cached again.
- **Expected behavior:** Complete scheduler read models must replace their prior document so absence is authoritative. Only the multi-location map should merge its single `stores.{sId}` entry to preserve sibling stores.
- **Root cause:** One merge-write policy was applied to both full-document snapshots and a genuinely partial multi-location map update, despite their different deletion/omission semantics.
- **Security/tenant impact:** No cross-tenant path was found. Document IDs and the multi-location map remain explicitly tenant/store scoped.
- **Data-integrity impact:** Owners could see analytics or health facts that were no longer present in the latest source-backed rebuild, including on reruns of the same local-date snapshot.
- **Public-truth impact:** Business Health is an owner-private read model and does not mutate public menu/store truth; the defect affected private operational truth.
- **Cache impact:** Server packet invalidation ran after the batch, but it could not correct stale fields preserved in Firestore; replacement writes make the next cache fill consistent.
- **Backward-compatibility impact:** The next successful scheduled rebuild removes stale unknown/optional fields without a separate migration. Write count, document IDs, retention timestamps, and the multi-location sibling-preserving merge remain unchanged.
- **Fix:** Removed merge options from current, snapshot, and analytics-index batch writes; retained `{ merge: true }` only for the per-store multi-location update.
- **Files changed:** `functions/src/ownerBusinessAssistant/ownerBusinessHealthWriters.ts`; `scripts/verification/verify-owner-business-assistant-hardening.ts`; Owner Business Assistant README/implementation/Firebase/validation docs; audit artifacts.
- **Regression test:** The focused verifier invokes the production writer with a captured Firestore batch, asserts replacement options for all three authoritative documents, asserts the multi-location merge, and proves an absent `analyticsTeaser` stays absent from the newly composed current payload.
- **Validation commands:** `npm run verify:owner-business-assistant`; `npm run verify:owner-business-health-boundary`; `npx eslint functions/src/ownerBusinessAssistant/ownerBusinessHealthWriters.ts scripts/verification/verify-owner-business-assistant-hardening.ts`; `npm --prefix functions run build` (rerun pending after concurrent analytics edit settles); broader type/docs/aggregate checks pending.
- **Validation result:** Both focused Business Health commands and touched-file lint passed. The concurrent Functions build failed only on unused declarations in the analytics agent's incomplete `healthSignalsComputation.ts` edit; no writer/test error was reported, and the exact-current package build will be rerun after handoff.
- **Re-audit pass:** Restart 183 Owner Business Health authoritative write trace; clean counter reset.

### AUDIT-OWNER-BUSINESS-HEALTH-READ-MODEL-001 — Raw persisted Business Health data crossed the response and cache boundary

- **Finding ID / severity / status:** AUDIT-OWNER-BUSINESS-HEALTH-READ-MODEL-001 / P2 / Closed locally; root/broader validation and hosted release evidence pending.
- **File and exact line/function:** `src/lib/ownerBusinessAssistant/server/buildOwnerBusinessAssistantContextPacket.ts::buildOwnerBusinessAssistantContextPacket()`; `src/lib/ownerBusinessAssistant/server/contextPacketCache.ts::readOwnerBusinessAssistantPacketCache()`; shared runtime contract in `src/lib/ownerBusinessAssistant/readModelBoundary.ts`; browser consumer gate in `src/lib/ownerBusinessAssistant/clientResponses.ts`.
- **Flow ID:** DF-OWNER-BUSINESS-HEALTH-READ-001; DF-OWNER-BUSINESS-HEALTH-CACHE-001; DF-OWNER-BUSINESS-HEALTH-RESPONSE-001.
- **Affected data structure:** Persisted current-health and analytics-index documents, cached `CachedOwnerBusinessAssistantPacket`, protected current/analytics JSON DTOs, and downstream SWR/browser state.
- **Producer / consumer / trigger:** Scheduler/Admin writers and Redis packet writes produce the data; context-packet builder, answer resolver, protected APIs, browser guards, desktop and mobile Business Health consumers read it; the trigger was the post-write downstream trace after Restart 183.
- **Observed behavior:** Firestore snapshots were cast directly from `DocumentData` to domain interfaces. The raw current-health object retained writer-added `kind` and `expiresAt` plus any legacy top-level/nested fields and was returned through `packet.health`; malformed arrays/maps could throw in metrics/template code before the browser guard. Stored `tId`/`sId` were not checked against the requested scope. Redis used `get<CachedOwnerBusinessAssistantPacket>()` as if the generic performed validation and did not verify packet/health identity against the requested cache key.
- **Expected behavior:** Runtime data must be parsed and projected before domain use or JSON serialization, internal persistence fields must not cross the DTO boundary, malformed/legacy rows must fail to bounded fallbacks, and cached identity must include every tenant/store/project dimension encoded by the key.
- **Root cause:** Compile-time interfaces and Redis generics were treated as runtime validators, and the browser response guard was downstream of server composition rather than being an authoritative shared schema.
- **Security/tenant impact:** No demonstrated cross-tenant read was found because writers/caches are server-owned, but a corrupted or stale cache entry was not independently scope-checked. The new boundary requires Firestore and Redis packet identities to match the requested tenant/store/project key.
- **Data-integrity impact:** Owners could receive internal/legacy fields or a 500/faulty packet from malformed persisted data instead of the intended not-ready/analytics-unavailable state.
- **Public-truth impact:** Business Health remains private and read-only; no public menu/store mutation path changed.
- **Cache impact:** Invalid, extra-field, or scope-mismatched cached packets now become observable cache misses; valid packets are recursively projected before reuse. Existing valid key format and TTL remain unchanged.
- **Backward-compatibility impact:** Valid version-1 documents and packets retain their supported fields. Unknown legacy fields are intentionally removed; malformed documents fall back until the next scheduler rebuild rather than being partially trusted.
- **Fix:** Added shared nested Zod schemas/parsers for current health and analytics, exact expected identity checks, schema projection before context composition, bounded invalid-row diagnostics, shared browser guard use, and a complete cached-packet parser that matches packet/health identity to the requested cache key.
- **Files changed:** `src/lib/ownerBusinessAssistant/readModelBoundary.ts`; `src/lib/ownerBusinessAssistant/server/buildOwnerBusinessAssistantContextPacket.ts`; `src/lib/ownerBusinessAssistant/server/contextPacketCache.ts`; `src/lib/ownerBusinessAssistant/clientResponses.ts`; focused verifier; Owner Business Assistant docs; changelog; audit artifacts.
- **Regression test:** The focused verifier covers storage-only/unknown top-level and nested fields, wrong persisted tenant identity, malformed required arrays, analytics projection, cache extra-field stripping, and cache-key/packet identity mismatch; source gates reject the retired raw Firestore casts.
- **Validation commands:** `npm run verify:owner-business-assistant`; `npm run verify:owner-business-health-boundary`; `npx eslint src/lib/ownerBusinessAssistant/readModelBoundary.ts src/lib/ownerBusinessAssistant/clientResponses.ts src/lib/ownerBusinessAssistant/server/buildOwnerBusinessAssistantContextPacket.ts src/lib/ownerBusinessAssistant/server/contextPacketCache.ts scripts/verification/verify-owner-business-assistant-hardening.ts`; root type/docs/aggregate checks pending.
- **Validation result:** Both focused Business Health gates and touched-file lint pass. Root TypeScript and broad validation await the concurrent analytics/messaging integration edits so the evidence reflects one settled tree.
- **Re-audit pass:** Restart 184 Owner Business Health persisted-response/cache boundary; clean counter reset.

### AUDIT-PUBLISH-VERIFICATION-AUTH-001 — Publish health Admin writes trusted stale claims and unscoped URLs

### AUDIT-FORCE-REPUBLISH-AUTH-001 — Force republish trusted stale platform authority and touched one arbitrary project

### AUDIT-PUBLISH-VERIFICATION-ASYNC-001 — Publish lifecycle delivery could be terminated after the callable returned

### AUDIT-AL-BILLING-PERMISSION-001 — Shared Razorpay routes bypassed Answerlattice billing permission

- **Finding ID / severity / status:** AUDIT-AL-BILLING-PERMISSION-001 / P1 / Closed locally; app deployment prohibited without explicit Vercel request.
- **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/lib/billing/billingAccess.ts::canManageAnswerlatticeBillingMutation()` and all eight routes under `src/app/api/razorpay/{create-subscription,verify-subscription,create-topup-order,verify-topup,cancel-subscription,pause-subscription,resume-subscription,upgrade-subscription}`; Answerlattice Billing UI -> shared APIs -> Razorpay -> Answerlattice Firestore.

The shared APIs skipped MenuList billing checks for Answerlattice and accepted `canUseAnswerlatticeManagement()`, which includes Manager. UI hiding was therefore the only billing restriction for that role.

Scope stayed within the Manager's workspace, but unauthorized financial and entitlement mutation was possible.
- **Fix / compatibility:** Every route now resolves the current persisted Answerlattice store, user membership, role definition, and permission through the existing access-control boundary and requires `canManageBilling: true`. Verification routes reject before provider reads; other routes reject before provider or financial mutation work. Platform authority and current authorized custom roles remain supported; MenuList behavior is unchanged.
- **Cost/cache/public impact:** Each Answerlattice mutation adds one store read plus a bounded current-user lookup (canonical query capped at two, legacy fallback only on miss). No cache/public-menu path, plan, price, collection, rule, index, or Functions logic changed.
- **Regression / validation:** `npm run verify:billing-entitlement-boundary` source-gates all eight routes and permission-before-provider order; `npm run test:answerlattice-access-user-scope` proves Owner allowed/default Manager denied; focused lint, docs links, tenant-safety/agent-readiness gates, `git diff --check`, and root TypeScript pass.

### AUDIT-TENANT-NAME-POST-COMMIT-001 — Derived-effect failure falsely failed committed tenant truth

- **ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-TENANT-NAME-POST-COMMIT-001 / P1 / Closed locally in restart 296. **Files/flow/structure:** `POST /api/tenants/name` -> transaction over `tenants/{tId}`, bounded tenant `stores`, `platformSummary/storesSummary` -> menu/store/client-store cache tags, digital-screen versions, Owner Business Assistant packets -> owner acknowledgement; tenant/store name public and owner truth.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** an authorized owner/platform rename commits the canonical tenant, up to 200 store mirrors, and summary atomically. The route then used synchronous tag calls plus chunked `Promise.all`. Any one cache, screen, or assistant failure threw into the outer catch, returned HTTP 500 with `committed:true`, and prevented later chunks/global tags from running. The browser was told the rename failed although retry could not roll it back, while later locations could remain stale.
- **Expected/root cause/impact:** the transaction is the success boundary. Derived effects must all be attempted, failures must be observable/recoverable, and committed truth must not receive a false failure response. Root cause was sharing one catch boundary between durable mutation and heterogeneous post-commit fanout. No cross-tenant mutation or billing impact was found. Public/owner truth could diverge temporarily across menu, screen, selector and assistant consumers, making this P1.
- **Fix/cost/compatibility:** `runTenantNamePostCommitEffects()` runs four effects per store in bounded chunks and both global tags with `Promise.allSettled`, counts every failure, retains the original first error, and continues all later work. The route logs stable `tenant_name_post_commit_effect_failed` once and returns success with `effectsPending`/`failedEffectCount`. Valid behavior and Firebase operation counts are unchanged; failure cases may retry through normal owner action while authoritative truth remains committed.
- **Regression/validation/deploy:** `test:tenant-name-post-commit` injects cache and screen failures across separate chunks, proves later store/global attempts, exact count, non-throwing completion and original-error observation. The multi-location source gate pins helper registration, all-settled/global behavior, route response and stable diagnostic. Exact root TypeScript and scoped ESLint pass. No Firebase infrastructure changed; Vercel deployment and authenticated browser/failure-injection proof remain external.

### AUDIT-NOTES-ATTACHMENT-AMBIGUOUS-COMMIT-001 — Response loss could delete attachments referenced by a committed note

- **ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-NOTES-ATTACHMENT-AMBIGUOUS-COMMIT-001 / P1 / Closed locally in restart 307. **Files/flow/structure:** `src/database/notes/index.ts`, `src/lib/notes/noteAttachmentBoundary.ts`; DF-NOTES-001; owner create/update -> attempt-unique scoped Storage uploads -> private `notes/{tId}/{sId}/{noteId}` finalization -> compensation or acknowledgement.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** `addNote` and `updateNote` uploaded new objects and then treated every rejected `setDoc`/transaction promise as proof the note write failed. Firestore may commit before the browser loses its acknowledgement. The catch then removed the new attempt objects (and create could delete the provisional note), leaving committed private truth with missing attachment bytes. The same defect affected create finalization and updates; no public DTO or cache was involved.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache impact:** destructive cross-service compensation requires authoritative proof that current exact-scope Firestore truth does not reference the new objects. Client promise rejection is not that proof. The defect did not bypass tenant authorization or expose another tenant, but it could corrupt owner-private note data. Notes remain private and have no public-truth/cache effects.

A pure projector classifies every uploaded URL as fully referenced, unreferenced, or partial. Full reference reconstructs success; none permits existing cleanup; partial, scope mismatch, or read failure retains objects and logs bounded ambiguity. A reconciled update defers old-object cleanup because the rejected transaction cannot safely return its transaction-current deletion set. Normal successful write/read counts are unchanged; only the thrown acknowledgement path adds one server read. Existing rows and URLs remain compatible.
- **Regression/validation/deploy:** the pure suite covers all/none/partial/empty commit projection in addition to identity and URL normalization. `npm run test:note-attachment-boundary`, the complete `npm run verify:storage-paths` suite (including the Storage emulator), `npm run verify:public-business-truth`, `npm run verify:menulist-api-tenant-safety`, exact root TypeScript and scoped ESLint pass. Hosted acknowledgement-loss injection and live orphan inventory remain external; clean counter is zero.

### AUDIT-AI-MENU-SESSION-IDENTITY-001 — Compact session IDs were syntactic rather than scope-deterministic at the rules boundary

- **ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-AI-MENU-SESSION-IDENTITY-001 / P1 / Closed locally in restart 229. **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/lib/ai-menu-manager/{idempotency,routeIds,schemas}.ts`, client/server DAL, command route, `firestore.rules`; selected tenant/store/project/date -> compact session document ID -> direct client create/server fallback merge.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** The application generated a custom hash but accepted any supplied string matching `amm_[a-f0-9]{24}`. The shared constructor requires normalized positive tenant/store IDs, a real UTC calendar date, and a required bounded project ID; the durable session type now matches that required Firestore field. Direct client, fallback route and server persistence independently require the supplied ID to match normalized scope/date/project; existing session identity is checked before merge; inbox rejects mismatched identity. Exact legacy hashed IDs computed by the prior algorithm remain readable/updatable for current in-flight sessions and proposal references, while rules reject new legacy creates. No collection, index, dependent rules read or scheduler was added.
- **Tests/closure:** Admin emulator rejects arbitrary IDs before creation and mismatched existing session merge. Rules emulator accepts exact v2 create/update, rejects arbitrary legacy create, mismatched v2 create, foreign-tenant create and direct proposal writes, and accepts an Admin-seeded legacy update for compatibility. The required MenuList QA Firestore-rules deploy read the correct local target and stopped at the Rules API with HTTP 403 caller permission before upload.

### AUDIT-AI-MENU-COMMAND-RETRY-IDENTITY-001 — Server-backed proposal retries did not bind the complete command identity

### AUDIT-AI-OPERATIONS-FILTER-PAGINATION-001 — Empty capped action scans hid older operation history

- **ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-AI-OPERATIONS-FILTER-PAGINATION-001 / P2 / Closed locally in restart 234. **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/app/api/ai-operations/route.ts::getActionFilteredDocs`, `src/lib/ai/operationHistoryQuery.ts::resolveAiOperationActionScanBoundary`, `src/database/aiOperations/index.tsx`, desktop `transactions/index.tsx`, and `MobileTransactionsScreen.tsx`; authenticated owner/platform history request -> nested tenant/store ledger query -> bounded action scan -> sanitized DTO -> cursor state -> desktop/mobile history.
- **Observed/root cause/impact:** The fallback action scan capped each request at 500 documents, but computed `hasMore` only when at least one matching row was returned. A zero-match capped window therefore declared the history exhausted even when older documents remained. A capped window with at most one result page also returned the last match as its cursor instead of the last scanned document, causing the next request to re-read the inspected gap. Both consumers independently treated every empty response as terminal. This could hide valid owner/platform operation truth and amplify Firestore reads; it did not cross tenant/store scope or expose disallowed fields.
- **Expected/invariants/security/data/public/cache/compatibility:** A scan ending because of the cost ceiling is nonterminal when a scan cursor exists. A buffered match must not be skipped; a fully inspected window must not be re-read. Empty continuation must be explicit on mobile so infinite loading cannot silently chain multiple 500-read windows. The response remains owner/platform allowlisted and tenant/store scoped. There is no persisted-data, public-output, cache, billing, rule, index, or legacy-document migration impact.
- **Fix/producers/consumers/cost:** The shared pure boundary distinguishes buffered matches, capped scans and true end-of-query; selects either the last returned match or full scan cursor; preserves `hasMore`; and reports `requiresManualContinuation` only for empty capped windows. The route and DAL carry that exact response field. Desktop retains the empty page cursor and Next state. Mobile disables `InfiniteScroll` and renders an explicit translated 44px Next action, for both initially empty and previously populated lists. The per-request ceiling remains 500 reads, and partial-match capped pages now avoid repeated gap reads.
- **Regression/validation/closure:** `scripts/verification/test-ai-operation-history-query.ts` covers zero-match cap, partial-match cap, buffered match, reached-end and empty-collection boundaries. `scripts/verification/verify-ai-accounting-hardening.js` pins route/DAL/desktop/mobile contracts and forbids the former `docs.length > 0` terminal predicate. `npm run test:ai-operation-history-query`, `npm run verify:ai-accounting`, `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false`, and scoped ESLint pass. Re-audit pass 234 closed the finding locally; Vercel deployment and authenticated browser/device pagination proof remain external and the clean counter is zero.

### AUDIT-PROJECT-PUBLISH-UPLOAD-001 — Project publish could overwrite bytes referenced by persisted state and admitted mismatched payloads

- **ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-PROJECT-PUBLISH-UPLOAD-001 / P1 / Closed locally in restart 244. **File/function/flow/structure:** `src/database/projects/index.ts`, `src/lib/menu/projectUploadIdentity.ts`, `src/lib/menu/projectUploadPayload.ts`, shared base64 uploader, project editor publish; owner file/data URL -> project payload validation -> tenant/store Storage object -> project transaction/server-linked save -> cache/snapshot consumers.

A failed uncommitted attempt can remove only its own object; an ambiguous server outcome retains it. Existing durable URLs remain compatible and shared font/document upload behavior is unchanged.

Project-specific broad type normalization was removed. Unique paths prevent overwrite and make definite pre-commit compensation safe; ambiguous linked results are not deleted. This adds no Firestore operation, collection, index, rule, Function or provider call, but can retain orphan bytes after ambiguous network outcomes until a future reference-aware retention cleanup exists.
- **Regression/validation/closure:** Pure tests cover unique attempts, normalization/truncation, empty attempt rejection, every admitted MIME, type mismatch, SVG rejection, malformed base64, signature mismatch, empty and oversized payloads. Project/editor, Storage-path/rules-emulator, public-truth, exact TypeScript and scoped lint gates pass. Hosted browser upload, real bucket metadata and ambiguous-network injection remain external; clean counter is zero.

### AUDIT-MEDIA-IMMUTABLE-OWNERSHIP-001 — Content-addressed prepared-media rollback could delete bytes referenced by another record

Regression fixtures cover hydrated/dehydrated equality, changed content and wrong dimensions.

### AUDIT-CC-CUELAYERS-IDEMPOTENCY-REPLAY-001 — Retry keys could alias different actors or payloads

- **ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-CC-CUELAYERS-IDEMPOTENCY-REPLAY-001 / P1 / Closed locally in restart 261. **Flow:** upload/autosave/repair/export retry -> idempotency claim -> durable effect/replay response.
- **Root cause/invariant/impact:** request-key-only reuse did not bind actor, action and normalized payload. A reused key could replay a different logical operation, while malformed persisted result IDs could be trusted.
- **Fix/evidence:** all four mutations derive actor/action/request hashes, fail closed on incompatible replay, validate stored result IDs/revisions/errors and finalize effects transactionally where Firestore truth is involved. Pure adversarial tests cover exact replay, actor/action/body mismatch and malformed records.

### AUDIT-CC-CUELAYERS-PERSISTED-BOUNDARIES-001 — Persisted jobs and layer indexes trusted incomplete runtime shapes

- **Fix/evidence:** strict record and layer-index projectors validate schema version, workspace/design/reconstruction identity, enums, ranges, cardinality, fallback references, immutable asset scope/hash/path and duplicate/conflict cases. Direct job reads no longer pass stored identity as its own expectation.

### AUDIT-CC-CUELAYERS-IMAGE-CONTAINER-LIMITS-001 — Structural image admission accepted trailing data and incomplete size limits

- **ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-CC-CUELAYERS-IMAGE-CONTAINER-LIMITS-001 / P2 / Closed locally in restart 261. **Flow:** uploaded or rendered bytes -> MIME/dimension projection -> Storage/export registration.
- **Root cause/invariant/impact:** filename/client MIME could diverge from bytes, PNG/JPEG/WebP structural probes tolerated trailing payloads, and export enforced long edge without the configured total-pixel ceiling.
- **Fix/evidence:** MIME, dimensions and canonical base64 are byte-derived; PNG `IEND`, JPEG `EOI` and WebP RIFF length must terminate exactly; upload and export enforce byte, edge and pixel ceilings. Tests cover PNG/JPEG/WebP VP8X/VP8L/VP8 plus malformed/trailing payloads.

### AUDIT-CC-CUELAYERS-FIREBASE-COST-001 — Boot and artifact handling performed avoidable work

- **Root cause/invariant/impact:** boot signed every design asset even when the saved document did not reference it, and mutation ordering could leave avoidable stale artifacts after deterministic conflicts.
- **Fix/evidence:** boot signs only durable referenced asset IDs; heavy JSON remains in Storage while Firestore retains compact pointers/state; final transactions prevent stale pointer commits and clean deterministic stale outputs. Current documented read/write accounting reflects layer-index/snapshot reads and atomic mutation reads/writes.

### AUDIT-CC-PACK-TEMPLATE-STALE-FACTS-001 — Saved templates could persist and reopen stale business content

### AUDIT-CC-PACK-TEMPLATE-FACT-GATE-001 — Fact requirements were inconsistent and never evaluated against current truth

### AUDIT-CC-PACK-TEMPLATE-STORAGE-RULES-RUNTIME-001 — Workspace template writes were denied by an unsupported recursive-path operation

The first emulator run reproduced the denial; the repaired full Storage emulator passes valid, cross-tenant, malformed-name/path/MIME and delete cases.

### AUDIT-CC-PACK-TEMPLATE-SEED-PUBLISH-001 — Platform seed publication was mutable, partially switchable and weakly targeted

### AUDIT-CC-OUTPUT-INTENT-DECISION-ALIGNMENT-001 — Output choices could relabel an unrelated recommendation

### AUDIT-CC-ACTION-IDEMPOTENCY-IDENTITY-001 — Campaign retry keys were not bound to actor or request payload

### AUDIT-CC-ACTION-TRANSACTION-001 — Concurrent ordinary actions could lose counters and result memory

Public-use actions also transaction-read current workspace truth and the compact source snapshot when required; blocked event and retry outcome commit in the same transaction.

### AUDIT-CC-ACTION-READ-COST-001 — Initial transaction repair duplicated campaign and source reads

- **Fix/evidence:** the obsolete branch was removed. Normal actions use one transactional campaign read; current workspace and source-snapshot reads occur only for public-use safety. This preserves correctness while avoiding duplicate Firebase reads.

### AUDIT-CC-ACTION-VERIFIER-DRIFT-001 — Aggregate verifier pinned the retired blocked-action batch shape

### AUDIT-MENU-EXTRACTION-LISTENER-IDENTITY-001 — A prior job result could execute under a newly tracked mobile job ID

- **ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-MENU-EXTRACTION-LISTENER-IDENTITY-001 / P1 / Closed locally in restart 266. **Files/functions/flow/structure:** `src/hooks/useMenuProcessingJob.ts::useMenuProcessingJob`; session-scoped active job ID -> Firestore listener -> completed/preview result -> desktop/mobile project mutation or review consumer.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** Firestore produces job A, the hook retains its snapshot in React state, and the caller switches to job B. Because effects run after render, the hook formerly returned job A during the B render; a listener error also retained A indefinitely. Desktop added a job-ID match before most effects, but mobile completion/review effects consumed the returned status/result without independently comparing `activeJob.id` to B. A completed or preview-ready A could therefore drive success, refresh, derived business defaults, or comparison setup while B/new project state was active.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache/compatibility:** Only a snapshot whose document ID equals the currently requested job ID may reach any derived state or consumer. The defect could apply prior extracted truth to the wrong owner project in browser state and trigger downstream owner mutations; server authorization still guarded final Firestore writes, so no cross-tenant read bypass was added beyond the separately repaired rules finding. Public/cache truth could become incorrect if a permitted wrong-project mutation completed. Existing valid listener behavior and job shapes remain unchanged.
- **Fix/regression/validation/closure:** the hook clears state before every new subscription and on listener error, then applies a render-time ID equality projection before deriving or returning any value. `npm run test:menu-processing-job-listener-boundary` proves the clear/error/ID-match contract and rejects derived-state bypass. Exact TypeScript and scoped ESLint pass; authenticated rapid project-switch/listener-denial browser injection remains external. No Firestore operation, rule, index, Function, cache, provider, or deployment target changed.

### AUDIT-EXTRACTION-MONITOR-RUNTIME-DATA-001 — Malformed persisted values could collapse or corrupt operational metrics

- **ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-EXTRACTION-MONITOR-RUNTIME-DATA-001 / P2 / Closed locally in restart 266. **Files/functions/flow/structure:** `src/database/ops/extraction.ts`, `src/lib/ops/extractionTypes.ts`; `menuImageProcessingJobs` and `MENULIST_AI_OPERATIONS` rows -> client aggregation -> platform desktop/mobile monitor.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** Functions and legacy/Admin writers produce timestamp, status, duration, quality, confidence, and charge fields. The DAL called arbitrary `toDate()` values without isolation, used truthiness and coercive addition on raw values, and accepted negative/out-of-range/non-finite numbers. One throwing timestamp could make the entire dashboard return empty fallback metrics; numeric strings could concatenate during reductions, while negative or extreme values distorted health, confidence, and spend.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache/compatibility:** every Firestore document is an untrusted runtime boundary. An invalid row must be excluded or have only its invalid metric omitted, and arithmetic must accept bounded finite values. This is internal platform-truth corruption, not a tenant authorization or public-output defect. Valid numeric/Timestamp/Date/legacy string-date behavior remains supported; `createdAt`/`completedAt` and pruned combined output are typed as `unknown` rather than falsely trusted `any`.
- **Fix/regression/validation/closure:** shared record/date/numeric projections isolate timestamp exceptions, reject coercive/negative/non-finite values, bound quality to 0–100 and page/count inputs, and compute cost from normalized charges. `npm run test:extraction-monitor-data-boundary` covers throwing timestamps, zero seconds, numeric strings, negative/NaN/out-of-range metrics, confidence counts, foreign actions, and charges. Exact TypeScript and scoped ESLint pass; live legacy-row sampling remains external. Reads, collections, indexes, rules, Functions, caches, billing writes, and public output are unchanged.

### AUDIT-EXTRACTION-PLATFORM-RETRY-AUTHORITY-001 — Founder retry used an incompatible owner tenant route

- **ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-EXTRACTION-PLATFORM-RETRY-AUTHORITY-001 / P1 / Closed locally in restart 266; hosted authenticated smoke pending. **Files/functions/flow/structure:** `src/database/ops/extraction.ts::retryExtractionJob`, `src/app/api/ops/extraction/jobs/[jobId]/retry/route.ts`, `src/lib/ops/extractionRetryBoundary.ts`; platform inspector -> failed job -> recovery authorization/validation -> active-job transaction -> replacement queue document -> extraction Function.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** the platform monitor can inspect failed jobs across tenants, but the retry helper re-read the job client-side and called `createMenuProcessingJob()`. Its ordinary owner API correctly requires the active session `tId`, `sId`, and `uId` to exactly match the original job, so a normal platform session retrying another tenant's job always failed despite the documented founder recovery control. The client also performed broad raw field/default coercion before sending source URLs back to the owner route.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache/compatibility:** platform-wide recovery must be explicit, current-authority checked, server-derived, tenant-safe, idempotency/concurrency protected, and must not weaken the owner route. A successful retry should preserve original owner/scope and create at most one active replacement. The former behavior was a serious operational pipeline failure rather than an authorization bypass. A replacement can eventually affect project/public truth through the existing worker, so canonical project and source ownership must be proven before enqueue; normal worker publication/cache behavior remains unchanged.
- **Fix/cost:** the client now sends only an encoded job ID to a no-store, same-origin, manual-redirect platform route, caps the response at 4KB, and accepts only a canonical replacement auto-ID. `withAuth` plus current persisted platform-user reauthorization, fail-closed per-operator `DATA_WRITE` rate limiting, SAFE_MODE, strict auto-ID admission, failed/retryable/max-three validation, exact project-destination and tenant/store/project/owner contract, duplicate-free bounded files/languages, supported MIME/size limits, private Storage-prefix validation, canonical nested project existence, Firestore sanitization, confirmed-success audit logging, and the existing active-job transaction precede the single replacement write. A normal successful recovery adds the current-user and SAFE_MODE checks, original job and project reads, and active transaction query before one job create; transaction contention can repeat its query.
- **Regression/validation/closure:** `npm run test:extraction-platform-retry-boundary` rejects completed/non-retryable/maxed/mismatched/duplicate/malformed jobs and foreign/non-Storage URLs, and source-proves platform/current-user/rate/safe-mode/project/sanitizer/transaction gates. Exact TypeScript and scoped ESLint pass. No Firestore rules/indexes or Cloud Functions changed, so no Firebase deploy applies; the new Next.js route requires an explicitly authorized Vercel deployment plus authenticated platform success/denial/concurrency smoke before runtime certification.

### AUDIT-MENU-EXTRACTION-JOB-RUNTIME-CONTRACT-001 — Owner listeners trusted arbitrary persisted job/result shapes

- **ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-MENU-EXTRACTION-JOB-RUNTIME-CONTRACT-001 / P2 / Closed locally in restart 267. **Files/functions/flow/structure:** `src/hooks/useMenuProcessingJob.ts::useMenuProcessingJob`, `src/lib/menu-extraction/menuProcessingJobStatusBoundary.ts`, `src/lib/firebase/menuProcessing.ts`; session job ID -> Firestore document -> lifecycle/result projection -> desktop/mobile completion or comparison consumer.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** Admin routes and the extraction worker produce job documents, while browser session state selects the document. The hook directly asserted `snapshot.data()` as `MenuProcessingJobStatus`; malformed/legacy status, project identity, numeric metrics, localized structures, array limits, category/item fields or file-result messages could therefore reach UI arithmetic and the comparison/write pipeline. A malformed session job ID could also reach Firestore reference construction before admission.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache/compatibility:** persisted Firestore data is untrusted at the browser boundary, regardless of TypeScript producer declarations. Only a canonical ID and a runtime-normalized lifecycle/result may reach consumers. This did not bypass Firestore rules, but malformed review truth could crash or corrupt a permitted project mutation and later public/cache truth. Valid worker shapes remain compatible, including pruned completed auto-save results; an invalid optional result does not reverse a server-confirmed save.
- **Fix/regression/validation/closure:** a pure boundary now validates project/status identity, bounded strict numbers, localized text, worker-aligned language/category/item/attribute limits, file results/messages, quality/provenance summaries, business-profile suggestions and supported project destination. Invalid preview payloads become a generic local failed state; missing/denied remembered jobs use the same terminal fallback so callers clear their active upload, while invalid optional metrics are excluded from completed jobs. The hook validates the auto-ID before subscribing, logs bounded invalid-data diagnostics and no longer casts raw snapshots. `npm run test:menu-processing-job-listener-boundary`, exact TypeScript and scoped ESLint pass. No Firestore read/write count, rule, index, Function, cache or deploy target changed; authenticated malformed-document browser injection remains external.

### AUDIT-MENU-EXTRACTION-COMPARISON-RELATION-001 — Orphan and colliding extracted items could enter project writes

- **ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-MENU-EXTRACTION-COMPARISON-RELATION-001 / P1 / Closed locally in restart 267. **Files/functions/flow/structure:** `src/lib/extraction/comparisonEngine.ts::runComparisonEngine`, `partitionUnsafeExtractedItems`, `buildApplyPlan`; retained `preview_ready.result.combinedData` -> client comparison -> owner approval -> project/outlet mutation -> public menu truth.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** worker hardening deliberately marks semantic integrity failures for review rather than failing extraction. The client comparison formerly resolved an orphan item to an empty category name but still approved it with its raw nonexistent category ID. Two different items with the same extraction ID in the same source file could generate the same persisted ID and overwrite/collapse during apply.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache/compatibility:** review may retain partial extraction evidence, but unsafe relations must not be present in the mutation plan. The defect could persist an orphan or replace a different item, creating incorrect public menu truth; normal apply already performs project cache invalidation, so the cache would faithfully publish the wrong state. Tenant authorization was unchanged.
- **Fix/regression/validation/closure:** comparison now partitions items before matching, excludes missing-category and duplicate source-file/ID pairs from every apply plan, and exposes both an ignored row and high-severity warning. Safe items and duplicates across different source files remain supported. The focused behavioral regression proves two unsafe rows produce zero writes while the safe row remains; exact TypeScript and scoped ESLint pass. Existing reads/writes, rules, indexes, Functions and invalidation paths are unchanged.

### AUDIT-MENU-EXTRACTION-REVIEW-METADATA-001 — Re-extraction dropped structured metadata for new items

- **ID/severity/status:** AUDIT-MENU-EXTRACTION-REVIEW-METADATA-001 / P2 / Closed locally in restart 267. **Files/functions/flow/structure:** `src/lib/extraction/comparisonEngine.types.ts`, `src/lib/extraction/comparisonEngine.ts::buildApplyPlan`, `src/lib/menu-extraction/menuProcessingJobStatusBoundary.ts`; worker combined item -> normalized preview -> standalone/outlet apply plan -> project file -> editor/public consumers.
- **Producer/consumer/trigger/observed:** the worker/redistribution contract carries variant attributes, tags, dietary tags, spice level and duration. `buildApplyPlan()` copied only ID, name, category, price and description for a newly approved re-extraction item, so the same extracted item had less public/customer decision truth when added through review than through first-extraction auto-save. Attribute active state was also absent.
- **Expected/root cause/security/data/public/cache/compatibility:** a safe new item must preserve the structured metadata already accepted from the extraction contract.
